name: Galileo
title: Galileo: Perceiving Physical Object Properties by Integrating a Physics Engine with Deep Learning
output: rigid-body scene + parameters
evaluation: Infers object mass and friction from real videos of simple physical events and predicts event outcomes, compared against human judgments.

generalization.note: Predicts outcomes of held-out physical events from inferred properties, but only in a narrow set of simple setups.

summary: Early analysis-by-synthesis model that infers object mass and friction from real videos by fitting a physics engine to tracked motion.
how: A Bullet-based generative model is fit to tracked trajectories with short MCMC runs; a deep network learns to invert it for fast property estimation.

lab_fit.note: Classic sampling-based sysid; adaptable to rigid scenes but no released code and hand-built scene setup.

name: ∇Sim (gradSim)
title: gradSim: Differentiable simulation for system identification and visuomotor control
institution: Montreal Robotics and Embodied AI Lab
output: mesh + physical parameters
evaluation: Recovers mass, friction, elasticity and cloth parameters from rendered videos of synthetic scenes and uses gradients for visuomotor control.

generalization.note: Uses identified parameters for control tasks, but tests are on synthetic scenes with known meshes.

summary: Combines differentiable multiphysics simulation with differentiable rendering to identify physical parameters directly from pixels.
how: Gradients of an image-space loss flow through a differentiable renderer and simulator to update physical parameters, given known object meshes.

lab_fit.note: Clear sysid formulation and code, but needs known geometry; mainly synthetic.

name: DANO
title: Differentiable Physics Simulation of Dynamics-Augmented Neural Objects
output: rigid-body scene + parameters — NeRF density + rigid dynamics
evaluation: Identifies mass and friction of NeRF-reconstructed objects from observed trajectories and re-simulates them for real-to-sim manipulation.

generalization.note: Re-simulates identified objects in new robotic interactions, on a small set of scenes.

summary: Augments NeRF-reconstructed objects with rigid-body dynamics so they can be simulated and their properties identified by gradient descent.
how: Contact geometry comes from the NeRF density field; a differentiable contact simulator optimizes mass and friction to match observed motion.

lab_fit.note: Real-to-sim rigid objects with re-simulation; small scope and no confirmed code.

name: RISP
title: RISP: Rendering-Invariant State Predictor with Differentiable Simulation and Rendering for Cross-Domain Parameter Estimation
output: rigid-body scene + parameters — known rigid/articulated/soft systems
evaluation: Estimates system parameters from videos rendered under unknown conditions (lighting, texture) on simulated tasks and a real-video example.

generalization.note: Targets robustness to the rendering domain gap, not prediction under new forces or initial states.

summary: Learns a rendering-invariant state predictor so physical parameters can be estimated from videos whose rendering settings are unknown.
how: A state predictor trained with domain randomization and a gradient-based regularizer maps frames to states; parameters are then optimized through differentiable simulation.

lab_fit.note: Addresses the render gap; requires a known simulator model of the system.

name: Virtual Elastic Objects
title: Virtual Elastic Objects
output: NeRF/particles + physical parameters
evaluation: Captures plush objects deformed by air streams with a multi-camera rig and evaluates re-simulation on held-out sequences and novel force inputs.

generalization.note: Re-simulates captured objects under new force inputs, evaluated mostly qualitatively and on held-out sequences.

summary: Builds virtual elastic objects from multi-view video of real deformations and re-simulates them under new forces.
how: Reconstructs a dynamic neural radiance field, then fits per-point material parameters with a differentiable physics simulator to match captured deformations.

lab_fit.note: Real-to-sim with re-simulation under new forces; needs a heavy multi-camera capture setup and no code release.

name: DiffCP
title: Differentiable Cloth Parameter Identification and State Estimation in Manipulation
output: spring-mass / particle model — cloth
evaluation: Identifies cloth parameters from RGB-D manipulation sequences and compares simulated cloth states with observations.

generalization.note: Uses identified parameters to predict cloth behaviour during subsequent manipulation, in limited robot settings.

summary: Real-to-sim cloth parameter identification during robot manipulation using a differentiable cloth simulator and RGB-D observations.
how: Minimizes the geometric gap between observed point clouds and simulated cloth states by gradient descent through the simulator.

lab_fit.note: Cloth-specific; needs RGB-D and a robot-interaction setup.

name: PAC-NeRF
title: PAC-NeRF: Physics Augmented Continuum Neural Radiance Fields for Geometry-Agnostic System Identification
output: NeRF/particles + physical parameters
evaluation: Recovers material parameters (e.g. Young's modulus, viscosity, friction angle) on synthetic multi-view videos and a few real captures.

generalization.note: Reports parameter error on the fitted sequences; no tests under new forces or initial states.

summary: Identifies geometry and continuum material parameters from multi-view videos by coupling a dynamic NeRF to a differentiable MPM.
how: An Eulerian-Lagrangian NeRF is advected by a differentiable MPM; rendering losses jointly optimize initial geometry, velocity and physical parameters.

lab_fit.note: Standard baseline that outputs a re-runnable MPM; public code and dataset.

name: Physics-guided SfT
title: Physics-guided Shape-from-Template: Monocular Video Perception through Neural Surrogate Models
output: mesh + physical parameters — cloth template
evaluation: Reconstructs cloth from monocular video given a template and reports geometric accuracy and recovered stiffness parameters.

generalization.note: Targets reconstruction of the observed sequence; no tests under new conditions.

summary: Recovers cloth shape and material parameters from monocular video using a differentiable renderer and a neural surrogate cloth simulator.
how: A pre-trained neural surrogate replaces the classical simulator; rendering losses back-propagate to stretching, shearing and bending parameters.

lab_fit.note: Template-based and focused on reconstruction, not predictive re-simulation.

name: DEFORM
title: Differentiable Discrete Elastic Rods for Real-Time Modeling of Deformable Linear Objects
output: spring-mass / particle model — discrete elastic rod
evaluation: Tracks and predicts wire/rope motion during real robot manipulation and compares prediction error with baselines.

generalization.note: Predicts deformable-linear-object motion under new robot manipulation actions over long horizons.

summary: Differentiable discrete elastic rod model with learned residual corrections for real-time modeling of ropes and cables from observations.
how: Rod parameters and a residual network are trained on real trajectories through a differentiable DER simulator.

lab_fit.note: Action-conditioned and predictive, but specific to linear deformables.

name: Differentiable SysID for Elastoplastic Manipulation
title: Differentiable Physics-based System Identification for Robotic Manipulation of Elastoplastic Materials
output: NeRF/particles + physical parameters — point-cloud particles
evaluation: Identifies dough-like material parameters from robot interactions and compares simulated and real point clouds on unseen manipulation motions.

generalization.note: Validates identified parameters on manipulation motions not used for identification.

summary: Identifies elastoplastic material parameters from robot interactions and depth observations with a differentiable MPM.
how: Point-cloud distances between real and simulated material after interactions are minimized through a differentiable MPM simulator.

lab_fit.note: Action-conditioned sysid with held-out motions; robotics-specific setup.

name: GIC
title: GIC: Gaussian-Informed Continuum for Physical Property Identification and Simulation
output: 3D Gaussians + physical parameters
evaluation: Benchmarks parameter recovery and future-state simulation on PAC-NeRF and Spring-Gaus data plus real captures.

generalization.note: Reports future-state simulation and digital-twin re-simulation, but conditions mostly mirror the fitted scene.

summary: Uses motion-factorized dynamic 3D Gaussians to provide dense continuum and surface supervision for differentiable-MPM property identification.
how: Dynamic Gaussians are converted to continuum particles via coarse-to-fine filling; MPM parameters are optimized against Gaussian-derived shapes and masks.

lab_fit.note: Strong sysid baseline with code; outputs a re-runnable MPM scene.

name: NeuMA
title: Neural Material Adaptor for Visual Grounding of Intrinsic Dynamics
output: 3D Gaussians + physical parameters — neural constitutive correction
evaluation: Evaluates trajectory and rendering accuracy on synthetic and real dynamic scenes and tests generalization to new objects and initial conditions.

generalization.note: Explicitly tests generalization to novel shapes, materials and initial conditions.

summary: Grounds intrinsic dynamics by adding a learned neural correction to an expert constitutive model, fit from visual observations.
how: A residual neural material adaptor corrects classical constitutive laws inside differentiable MPM; Particle-GS renders particles for image-space supervision.

lab_fit.note: Has code and explicit generalization tests; fits hidden-condition evaluation.

name: PhysAvatar
title: PhysAvatar: Learning the Physics of Dressed 3D Avatars from Visual Observations
output: mesh + physical parameters — garment mesh + Gaussians
evaluation: Evaluates novel-view and novel-motion rendering of dressed humans against avatar baselines on multi-view captures.

generalization.note: Animates avatars with novel body motions using the identified garment physics.

summary: Estimates garment physical parameters of a dressed human from multi-view video with inverse rendering and inverse physics.
how: Tracks garment meshes, optimizes cloth material parameters through a physics simulator, and uses physically based rendering for appearance.

lab_fit.note: Human-avatar specific capture pipeline.

name: Spring-Gaus
title: Reconstruction and Simulation of Elastic Objects with Spring-Mass 3D Gaussians
output: spring-mass / particle model — with 3D Gaussians
evaluation: Evaluates reconstruction and future-frame prediction on synthetic and real elastic objects falling and bouncing.

generalization.note: Predicts future frames beyond the fitting window and shows simulation under new initial conditions qualitatively.

summary: Represents elastic objects as 3D Gaussians attached to a spring-mass model whose stiffness is learned from multi-view video.
how: Reconstructs static 3D Gaussians, anchors them to spring-mass points, and optimizes spring parameters through a differentiable simulator to match the video.

lab_fit.note: Outputs a simulatable spring-mass model; public code and data.

name: AS-DiffMPM
title: Gaussian-Augmented Physics Simulation and System Identification with Complex Colliders
output: 3D Gaussians + physical parameters
evaluation: Evaluates physical-parameter estimation when objects collide with non-planar rigid bodies, interfaced with several novel-view-synthesis backends.

generalization.note: Focus is identification accuracy with complex colliders, not new-condition prediction.

summary: Extends differentiable-MPM system identification to objects interacting with arbitrarily shaped rigid colliders.
how: Adds differentiable collision handling to MPM so geometry, appearance and material parameters can be optimized end-to-end with Gaussian rendering.

lab_fit.note: Code available; supports richer contact scenes.

name: MASIV
title: MASIV: Toward Material-Agnostic System Identification from Videos
output: 3D Gaussians + physical parameters — neural constitutive model
evaluation: Evaluates geometric accuracy, rendering quality and generalization on multi-material system-identification benchmarks.

generalization.note: Reports generalization ability to new conditions, but on simulated benchmarks.

summary: Material-agnostic system identification that learns a neural constitutive model from video instead of assuming a hand-crafted material law.
how: Reconstructs dense continuum particle trajectories as geometric guidance, then trains a neural constitutive model inside differentiable MPM.

lab_fit.note: Outputs a re-runnable MPM with learned material; code available.

name: MPMAvatar
title: MPMAvatar: Learning 3D Gaussian Avatars with Accurate and Robust Physics-Based Dynamics
output: 3D Gaussians + physical parameters — garment mesh
evaluation: Evaluates geometry and appearance of animated loose garments on ActorsHQ and 4D-DRESS against PhysAvatar and avatar baselines.

generalization.note: Animates avatars under novel body motions with identified garment physics.

summary: Learns physically simulatable 3D Gaussian avatars with loose garments, identifying garment parameters for an MPM cloth solver.
how: Tracked garment meshes supervise optimization of density, stiffness and a rest-geometry term in a tailored anisotropic MPM; Gaussians render appearance.

lab_fit.note: Human-avatar specific.

name: PhysTwin
title: PhysTwin: Physics-Informed Reconstruction and Simulation of Deformable Objects from Videos
output: spring-mass / particle model — with 3D Gaussians
evaluation: Evaluates reconstruction/resimulation, future prediction and generalization to unseen hand interactions on real rope, cloth and plush videos.

generalization.note: Tests future prediction and simulation under novel interactions, and uses the twin for model-based planning.

summary: Builds interactive digital twins of deformable objects from sparse-view videos of hand interaction using spring-mass physics and Gaussians.
how: Generative shape completion plus a two-stage optimization (zero-order for global parameters, then first-order dense spring stiffness) fits a spring-mass model.

lab_fit.note: Re-runnable, action-conditioned twin with code; tested under unseen interactions.

name: Seeing the Wind
title: Seeing the Wind from a Falling Leaf
output: 3D Gaussians + physical parameters — plus force field
evaluation: Recovers wind/force fields from synthetic and real videos and demonstrates physics-based video generation and editing.

generalization.note: Applies recovered forces to edit or generate new motions, evaluated mostly qualitatively.

summary: Recovers invisible force fields such as wind, together with geometry and physical properties, from videos of moving objects.
how: An end-to-end differentiable inverse-graphics pipeline jointly optimizes object geometry, physical properties and a force representation by backpropagation.

lab_fit.note: Novel force-inference target; code not confirmed.

name: Vid2Sim
title: Vid2Sim: Generalizable, Video-based Reconstruction of Appearance, Geometry and Physics for Mesh-free Simulation
output: 3D Gaussians + physical parameters — mesh-free reduced sim
evaluation: Evaluates geometry, appearance and physical-parameter accuracy on synthetic and real elastic-object videos against optimization baselines.

generalization.note: Re-simulates recovered objects; limited tests under new forces.

summary: Feed-forward network estimates physics from video, followed by a quick optimization refining appearance, geometry and elastic parameters.
how: A generalizable network predicts initial geometry and material; a lightweight differentiable mesh-free (LBS) simulation then refines everything in minutes.

lab_fit.note: Fast, has code, and outputs a simulatable object.

name: CausalGS
title: CausalGS: Learning Physical Causality of 3D Dynamic Scenes with Gaussian Representations
output: 3D Gaussians + physical parameters
evaluation: Evaluates future trajectory prediction and rendering on multi-view dynamic-scene benchmarks.

generalization.note: Predicts future trajectories beyond the fitted window.

summary: Learns causal scene dynamics from multi-view video by jointly inferring initial velocity fields and intrinsic material properties.
how: An inverse-physics module infers initial velocities and material properties, which drive a differentiable simulator as physics regularization.

lab_fit.note: Code available; new and less validated.

name: KnockGS
title: KnockGS: Interaction-Grounded Calibration of Physical Gaussian Representations
output: 3D Gaussians + physical parameters
evaluation: Compares recovered elasticity/density scales with hidden ground truth and re-simulates under held-out interactions using particle trajectories, response curves and rendering.

generalization.note: Freezes the estimate and tests it on interactions that differ in direction and magnitude.

summary: Estimates elasticity and density scales of a Gaussian object from its response to a known applied force, then tests on unseen interactions.
how: Temporal response features from observed dynamics are mapped to material scales, which are written back into the simulator and evaluated on held-out interactions.

lab_fit.note: Its protocol (frozen estimate, held-out interactions) closely matches hidden-condition scoring.

name: MonoPhysics
title: MonoPhysics: Estimating Geometry, Appearance, and Physical Parameters from Monocular Videos
output: 3D Gaussians + physical parameters
evaluation: Evaluates future prediction and Young's-modulus recovery on Vid2Sim data, real captures and a new elastic/plasticine dataset.

generalization.note: Reports future prediction beyond observed frames; no new-force tests stated.

summary: Monocular inverse physics for deformable objects that jointly optimizes geometry, appearance and physical parameters.
how: Scene re-parameterization, physics-aware geometry refinement and a differentiable position map couple 3DGS to a differentiable simulator without multi-view constraints.

lab_fit.note: Monocular input and future-prediction focus; code released.

name: DreamPhysics
title: DreamPhysics: Learning Physics-Based 3D Dynamics with Video Diffusion Priors
output: 3D Gaussians + physical parameters
evaluation: Compares generated dynamics with prior physics-generation methods through user studies and qualitative results.

generalization.note: No evaluation against real dynamics or new conditions.

summary: Learns physical parameters of 3D Gaussian scenes by score distillation from video diffusion models.
how: Motion-aware score distillation from a video diffusion model supervises material parameters in a differentiable MPM.

lab_fit.note: Parameters fit to a generative prior, not observations.

name: Feature Splatting
title: Feature Splatting: Language-Driven Physics-Based Scene Synthesis and Editing
output: 4D video / animation — semantic Gaussians
evaluation: Demonstrates language-queried object selection and physics-based edits on real scenes, evaluated qualitatively.

generalization.note: Materials are assigned from language queries; no comparison to real dynamics.

summary: Distills vision-language features into 3D Gaussians so text queries can select objects and assign materials for physics simulation.
how: Foundation-model features are splatted into Gaussians; text-selected parts receive material settings and are simulated with MPM.

lab_fit.note: Editing tool; parameters chosen from language, not identified.

name: Gaussian Splashing
title: Gaussian Splashing: Unified Particles for Versatile Motion Synthesis and Rendering
output: 4D video / animation — Gaussians + PBD particles
evaluation: Shows qualitative solid-fluid interaction animations and rendering of reconstructed scenes.

generalization.note: Parameters are user-specified; no comparison to real dynamics.

summary: Unifies 3D Gaussians with position-based dynamics to animate solids and fluids together, including fluid surface rendering.
how: Gaussians become PBD particles for solids and fluids; normals and specular terms are added for realistic fluid rendering.

lab_fit.note: Animation tool; no parameter identification.

name: Phys4DGen
title: Phys4DGen: Physics-Compliant 4D Generation with Multi-Material Composition Perception
output: 3D Gaussians + physical parameters — multi-material
evaluation: Compares generated 4D content with prior physics-based 4D generation methods via metrics and user studies.

generalization.note: No evaluation against real future observations.

summary: 4D generation that automatically perceives multi-material composition and assigns physical properties before simulation.
how: Segments the 3D object into material parts, infers material types and properties with foundation models, and simulates with MPM.

lab_fit.note: Generation-oriented; no observation-grounded identification.

name: PhysDreamer
title: PhysDreamer: Physics-Based Interaction with 3D Objects via Video Generation
output: 3D Gaussians + physical parameters — material field
evaluation: Evaluates realism of interactive dynamics on real objects through a user study against baselines.

generalization.note: Simulates responses to new user-applied forces, judged by humans rather than ground truth.

summary: Distills a spatially varying material field for static 3D objects from video-generation priors to enable interactive dynamics.
how: A video generation model produces plausible motion of the object; a differentiable MPM optimizes the Young's modulus field and initial velocity to match it.

lab_fit.note: Produces a re-runnable MPM with parameters; parameters come from generated, not observed, video.

name: PhysFlow
title: PhysFlow: Unleashing the Potential of Multi-modal Foundation Models and Video Diffusion for 4D Dynamic Physical Scene Simulation
output: 3D Gaussians + physical parameters
evaluation: Evaluates 4D simulations on synthetic and real scenes with perceptual metrics and user studies against prior physics-generation baselines.

generalization.note: No evaluation under new forces or against real future frames.

summary: Initializes material types and parameters with a multimodal foundation model and refines them with optical-flow guidance from video diffusion.
how: MLLM queries give initial materials; a differentiable MPM is refined so rendered optical flow matches flow from video-diffusion-generated clips.

lab_fit.note: Prior-driven parameters; no observation-grounded prediction.

name: PhysGaussian
title: PhysGaussian: Physics-Integrated 3D Gaussians for Generative Dynamics
output: 4D video / animation — 3D Gaussians as MPM particles
evaluation: Shows qualitative simulations of reconstructed scenes across materials, with comparisons to mesh-based pipelines.

generalization.note: Material parameters are set manually; no prediction against real dynamics.

summary: Treats 3D Gaussians as continuum particles so reconstructed scenes can be simulated with MPM and rendered directly.
how: Gaussian kernels carry MPM state and deform with the simulated deformation gradient; internal filling and anisotropy regularization stabilize results.

lab_fit.note: Forward-simulation foundation; parameters are hand-set, so it needs an identification layer to serve as a baseline.

name: PhysGen
title: PhysGen: Rigid-Body Physics-Grounded Image-to-Video Generation
output: 4D video / animation — 2D rigid-body scene
evaluation: Evaluates physical realism and appearance of generated videos with human studies and image/video metrics against video-generation baselines.

generalization.note: Generates videos under user-specified forces and torques, judged by humans.

summary: Image-to-video generation that simulates 2D rigid-body dynamics of segmented objects under user-specified forces, then renders and refines.
how: Perception estimates object geometry, materials and physical parameters from the image; a rigid-body simulator rolls out motion; diffusion-based rendering refines frames.

lab_fit.note: Explicit simulator with force inputs; parameters guessed by perception, 2D only.

name: Physics3D
title: Physics3D: Learning Physical Properties of 3D Gaussians via Video Diffusion
output: 3D Gaussians + physical parameters — elastic + viscous
evaluation: Evaluates generated dynamics with user studies and CLIP-based metrics against prior physics-generation methods.

generalization.note: No tests against real observations.

summary: Learns viscoelastic physical properties of 3D Gaussians by distilling video-diffusion priors through an MPM simulator.
how: A viscoelastic MPM with learnable parameters is rendered and optimized with score distillation from a video diffusion model.

lab_fit.note: Generative-prior fit; no observation-grounded prediction.

name: PhysMotion
title: PhysMotion: Physics-Grounded Dynamics From a Single Image
output: 4D video / animation
evaluation: Shows physically grounded single-image animations and compares visual quality with video-generation baselines.

generalization.note: Supports user-specified input conditions (forces, materials), judged visually.

summary: Generates physics-grounded dynamics from a single image by simulating a reconstructed 3D Gaussian with MPM and refining with video diffusion.
how: Single-image 3D reconstruction yields Gaussians; differentiable MPM simulates them under input conditions; a diffusion model refines the coarse rendering.

lab_fit.note: Generation pipeline; parameters user-set.

name: Sim Anything
title: Efficient Physics Simulation for 3D Scenes via MLLM-Guided Gaussian Splatting
output: 3D Gaussians + physical parameters — material distribution
evaluation: Compares motion realism with video-prior-based methods through quantitative metrics and user studies.

generalization.note: No tests against real dynamics.

summary: Endows static 3D Gaussian objects with dynamics by predicting physical properties with a multimodal LLM instead of video distillation.
how: MLLM-P3 predicts mean properties zero-shot, MPDP predicts their spatial distribution, and adaptive particle sampling feeds an efficient MPM.

lab_fit.note: Feed-forward property guessing; no identification from observations.

name: Sync4D
title: Sync4D: Video Guided Controllable Dynamics for Physics-Based 4D Generation
output: 4D video / animation — generated 3D Gaussians
evaluation: Shows motion transfer from casual reference videos (humans, quadrupeds, articulated objects) to generated 3D Gaussians, compared qualitatively and with user preference.

generalization.note: Transfers observed motion; no prediction under new conditions.

summary: Transfers motion from casually captured reference videos onto generated 3D Gaussians using physics simulation.
how: Blend-skinning shape reconstruction extracts reference motion; physical simulation drives matched target shapes, optimized with a displacement loss.

lab_fit.note: Motion transfer, not system identification.

name: VR-GS
title: VR-GS: A Physical Dynamics-Aware Interactive Gaussian Splatting System in Virtual Reality
output: 4D video / animation — interactive Gaussians
evaluation: Evaluates interactive VR manipulation of reconstructed scenes with a user study and runtime measurements.

generalization.note: Interactive, but parameters are hand-set; no real-dynamics validation.

summary: Real-time VR system that lets users interact with physically simulated 3D Gaussian scenes.
how: Segments Gaussians into objects, embeds them in tetrahedral cages, and drives them with XPBD for real-time deformation and collision.

lab_fit.note: Interaction system; no identification or prediction scoring.

name: OmniPhysGS
title: OmniPhysGS: 3D Constitutive Gaussians for General Physics-Based Dynamics Generation
output: 3D Gaussians + physical parameters — per-Gaussian constitutive model
evaluation: Evaluates generated multi-material dynamics with CLIP-based metrics and user studies against prior physics-generation baselines.

generalization.note: No tests against real dynamics.

summary: Learns per-Gaussian constitutive models as mixtures of expert material laws, supervised by video-diffusion priors and text prompts.
how: A physics-guided network predicts strain/stress per Gaussian from expert constitutive models; MPM rollouts are rendered and optimized with video diffusion guidance.

lab_fit.note: Generative-prior supervision; the constitutive-mixture idea could be reused in sysid.

name: PhyMAGIC
title: PhyMAGIC: Physical Motion-Aware Generative Inference with Confidence-guided LLM
output: 3D Gaussians + physical parameters
evaluation: Evaluates physical property inference and motion consistency against video-diffusion and physics-generation baselines.

generalization.note: No tests under new conditions against ground truth.

summary: Training-free single-image framework that infers physical properties with an LLM and image-to-video diffusion, then simulates them.
how: Image-to-video diffusion and confidence-guided LLM reasoning propose properties; a differentiable MPM on 3D Gaussians refines them iteratively.

lab_fit.note: Prior-driven; no observation-grounded hidden-condition prediction.

name: PhysAnimator
title: PhysAnimator: Physics-Guided Generative Cartoon Animation
output: 4D video / animation — 2D cartoon
evaluation: Evaluates generated cartoon animations with user studies and comparisons to video-generation baselines.

generalization.note: Supports user-defined forces and sketches, evaluated visually.

summary: Generates physically plausible cartoon animations from static anime illustrations by simulating 2D deformable bodies and rendering with diffusion.
how: Segments the drawing into deformable meshes, simulates them under user forces, and uses sketch-guided video diffusion to render final frames.

lab_fit.note: Stylized 2D animation; not a real-to-sim method.

name: PhysCtrl
title: PhysCtrl: Generative Physics for Controllable and Physics-Grounded Video Generation
output: 4D video / animation — 3D point trajectories
simulator: learned generative physics (diffusion trained on simulator data)
evaluation: Compares generated trajectories and videos with video-generation baselines on visual quality and physical plausibility, including user studies.

generalization.note: Controls videos via physics parameters and applied forces; ground-truth checks are on synthetic data.

summary: Physics-grounded image-to-video generation conditioned on material parameters and forces via a diffusion model over point trajectories.
how: A trajectory diffusion model trained on 550K simulated animations generates 3D point motion, which drives a pretrained image-to-video model.

lab_fit.note: Accepts force/parameter inputs; physics is a learned surrogate rather than an explicit simulator.

name: PhysGen3D
title: PhysGen3D: Crafting a Miniature Interactive World from a Single Image
output: 4D video / animation — 3D scene with physical parameters
evaluation: Compares generated videos with image-to-video models via user studies and VLM-based physical-realism scoring.

generalization.note: Generates outcomes under user-specified initial conditions, evaluated perceptually.

summary: Builds an interactive 3D scene from a single image, with geometry, materials and lighting, then simulates and renders user-specified dynamics.
how: Image-to-3D, VLM-estimated physical properties and MPM simulation are combined with physically based rendering to produce videos.

lab_fit.note: Explicit simulator with controllable inputs; parameters come from priors, not observation.

name: PhysGM
title: PhysGM: Large Physical Gaussian Model for Feed-Forward 4D Synthesis
output: 3D Gaussians + physical parameters
evaluation: Evaluates feed-forward 4D synthesis quality and speed against optimization-based physics generation methods.

generalization.note: No evaluation against real dynamics under new conditions.

summary: Feed-forward model that predicts 3D Gaussians and physical properties from a single image for fast physics-based 4D synthesis.
how: A large model jointly predicts Gaussians and material parameters in one forward pass, then simulates them with MPM.

lab_fit.note: Fast feed-forward parameter prediction could serve as an initializer baseline.

name: WonderPlay
title: WonderPlay: Dynamic 3D Scene Generation from a Single Image and Actions
output: 4D video / animation — dynamic 3D scene
simulator: hybrid: coarse physics sim (MPM/rigid) + video diffusion
evaluation: Evaluates action-conditioned dynamic scenes with user studies and VLM scoring against physics- and video-based baselines.

generalization.note: Takes user actions (e.g. forces, wind) as input, evaluated perceptually.

summary: Generates action-conditioned dynamic 3D scenes from a single image by combining physics simulation with video generation.
how: A coarse physics simulation produces 3D dynamics that condition a video generator; the generated video then refines the 3D scene in a closed loop.

lab_fit.note: Action-conditioned; but final dynamics come from generative refinement.

name: MotionPhysics
title: MotionPhysics: Learnable Motion Distillation for Text-Guided Simulation
output: 3D Gaussians + physical parameters
evaluation: Evaluates over thirty scenarios (real, designed and AI-generated objects) with perceptual metrics and user studies.

generalization.note: Parameters follow text prompts; no ground-truth prediction tests.

summary: Infers physical parameters for an existing 3D scene from a text prompt using MLLM initialization and motion distillation from video diffusion.
how: An MLLM proposes bounded material values; a learnable motion-distillation loss extracts motion priors from video diffusion to refine them through differentiable simulation.

lab_fit.note: Text-guided generation, not observation-grounded.

name: PowerSim
title: PowerSim: Differentiable Physics Simulation and Rendering with Power Diagrams
output: 3D Gaussians + physical parameters — PowerFoam primitives
evaluation: Demonstrates interactive simulation, spatially varying material-field recovery, scene compositing and ray-traced reflections on real and synthetic scenes.

generalization.note: Simulates scenes under new user interactions; material recovery shown on limited cases.

summary: Couples PowerFoam power-diagram scenes directly to MPM so simulated motion drives geometry and appearance differentiably.
how: Each power-diagram primitive maps to MPM-tracked quantities, giving differentiable dynamics and rendering without an auxiliary representation.

lab_fit.note: Differentiable sim and render could support identification; new and less validated.

name: Resonance4D
title: Resonance4D: Frequency-Domain Motion Supervision for Preset-Free Physical Parameter Learning in 4D Dynamic Physical Scene Simulation
output: 3D Gaussians + physical parameters — part-level
evaluation: Evaluates physical fidelity, motion quality and training cost on synthetic and real scenes against video-diffusion-supervised methods.

generalization.note: No tests under new forces or held-out conditions.

summary: Couples 3DGS with MPM and replaces dense video-diffusion supervision with spatial plus frequency-domain motion supervision for full material parameter learning.
how: Text-prompted segmentation splits Gaussians into parts; full material parameters are optimized with structural and spectral motion-consistency losses.

lab_fit.note: Generation-oriented; supervision is not hidden-condition prediction.

name: Ditto
title: Ditto: Building Digital Twins of Articulated Objects from Interaction
output: articulated asset (URDF/MJCF) — part meshes + joint parameters
evaluation: Part geometry (Chamfer) and joint axis/pivot/state errors on Shape2Motion objects plus qualitative real-world twins loaded into a simulator.

generalization.note: Recovered joints let the twin be actuated to unseen joint states, but these are not scored against held-out real motions.

summary: Feed-forward network that builds an articulated digital twin from point clouds captured before and after one interaction.
how: A PointNet++/ConvONet encoder fuses the two observations into dense features; implicit decoders predict part occupancy, segmentation and per-point joint type, axis and state.

lab_fit.note: Clean observation-to-asset mapping; the exported twin can be re-articulated and scored on hidden joint configurations.

name: Ditto in the House
title: Ditto in the House: Building Articulation Models of Indoor Scenes through Interactive Perception
output: articulated asset (URDF/MJCF) — room-scale articulated objects
evaluation: Articulated-object discovery and joint estimation accuracy in simulated houses and real-world scenes.

generalization.note: Evaluates recovered articulation, not behaviour of the twin under new interactions.

summary: Robot autonomously finds, pokes and models all articulated objects in a room to build a scene-level articulation model.
how: Affordance prediction proposes interaction points; the robot interacts and Ditto-style inference on before/after observations recovers each object's articulation, with the two stages refining each other.

lab_fit.note: Needs an active robot in the loop for interaction, which a passive observation-only platform cannot supply.

name: PARIS
title: PARIS: Part-level Reconstruction and Motion Analysis for Articulated Objects
output: articulated asset (URDF/MJCF) — part implicit surfaces + one joint
evaluation: Part/object Chamfer distance and joint axis/position/state errors on PartNet-Mobility objects and real scans.

generalization.note: Can render unseen intermediate articulation states, but only for the single observed joint.

summary: Self-supervised per-object optimization that separates static and movable parts and recovers joint motion from multi-view images of two states.
how: Two NeRF-style part fields are optimized jointly with a rigid motion between the two states; the motion is converted to a revolute or prismatic joint.

lab_fit.note: Pure observation input and an explicit joint model make it an easy baseline for predicting hidden articulation states.

name: Digital Twin ART
title: Neural Implicit Representation for Building Digital Twins of Unknown Articulated Objects
output: articulated asset (URDF/MJCF) — multi-part meshes + joints
evaluation: Part geometry and joint parameter errors on synthetic multi-part objects and real RGB-D scans, compared with PARIS and Ditto.

generalization.note: Twin can be posed to new joint states but evaluation only checks recovered parameters.

summary: Builds digital twins of unknown multi-part articulated objects from RGB-D scans in two articulation states, without shape priors.
how: Reconstructs each state as a neural implicit field, then optimizes part segmentation and joint parameters so that the two states are consistent.

lab_fit.note: Observation-only, outputs an explicit kinematic model that can be rolled out under hidden joint commands.

name: Robot See Robot Do (RSRD)
title: Robot See Robot Do: Imitating Articulated Object Manipulation with Monocular 4D Reconstruction
output: articulated asset (URDF/MJCF) — part-segmented Gaussian model with tracked part poses
evaluation: Part-pose tracking quality and real bimanual robot success at reproducing demonstrated part motions on 9 objects (60% end-to-end).

generalization.note: Robot reproduces the demonstrated motion from new object poses; no new articulation behaviours are tested.

summary: Builds a part-level 4D model of an articulated object from a static scan and one monocular human demo video, then makes a robot replicate the part motion.
how: A GARField-segmented Gaussian splat with DINO feature fields is fit to the video by differentiable rendering (4D-DPM); the recovered part trajectories drive bimanual grasp and motion planning.

lab_fit.note: Recovers part trajectories rather than an explicit joint model, so predicting hidden conditions needs extra kinematic fitting.

name: URDFormer
title: URDFormer: A Pipeline for Constructing Articulated Simulation Environments from Real-World Images
output: articulated asset (URDF/MJCF) — objects and kitchen scenes
evaluation: Kinematic-structure accuracy of predicted URDFs on internet images and real-to-sim-to-real policy success on a real robot.

generalization.note: Policies trained in the generated URDFs are tested on the real object, but the twin itself is not checked against unseen real motions.

summary: Transformer that turns a single real image of an object or kitchen into an articulated URDF scene for robot learning.
how: Detected part boxes are fed to a transformer trained on paired data synthesized with controllable text-to-image generation, which predicts part types, joints and hierarchy as URDF.

lab_fit.note: Single-image prior gives plausible but category-level joints; easy to run but weak on exact dynamics.

name: ArtGS
title: ArtGS: Building Interactable Replicas of Complex Articulated Objects via Gaussian Splatting
output: articulated asset (URDF/MJCF) — Gaussian parts + part meshes + joints
evaluation: Joint parameter error and part mesh reconstruction on synthetic and real multi-part objects, including a new complex-object benchmark.

generalization.note: Replicas can be driven to unseen joint configurations, but scoring focuses on recovered parameters.

summary: Reconstructs complex multi-part articulated objects as interactable Gaussian-splat replicas from multi-view observations of two states.
how: Canonical 3D Gaussians with coarse-to-fine initialization are aligned across states, and a skinning-inspired part-dynamics module learns part assignment and joint motion.

lab_fit.note: Observation-only per-object optimization with explicit joints; can be re-posed for hidden-condition queries.

name: Articulate AnyMesh
title: Articulate AnyMesh: Open-Vocabulary 3D Articulated Objects Modeling
output: articulated asset (URDF/MJCF)
evaluation: Articulation quality on open-vocabulary meshes against prior methods, and sim-learned manipulation skills transferred to a real robot.

generalization.note: Assets are used to train new skills transferred to real, but the twin is not scored on unseen real motions.

summary: Turns any rigid 3D mesh into an articulated asset with open-vocabulary part segmentation and VLM-guided joint estimation.
how: VLM visual prompting segments functional parts and infers joint type and axis from geometric cues, then exports an articulated model.

lab_fit.note: Requires a mesh as input, so a reconstruction step must precede it on an observation-only platform.

name: Articulate-Anything
title: Articulate-Anything: Automatic Modeling of Articulated Objects via a Vision-Language Foundation Model
output: articulated asset (URDF/MJCF) — URDF via generated code
evaluation: Joint/link prediction success on PartNet-Mobility against Real2Code and URDFormer, plus training manipulation policies in the generated assets.

generalization.note: Generated assets are used to train policies, but not validated against unseen real interactions.

summary: VLM actor-critic agent that writes, renders and critiques code to turn text, images or videos into articulated URDF assets.
how: Mesh retrieval picks parts; a VLM actor writes link and joint code, the result is simulated and rendered, and a VLM critic compares it to the input and requests fixes.

lab_fit.note: Agentic code-writing loop maps directly onto an observation-in, simulation-code-out baseline.

name: AutoURDF
title: AutoURDF: Unsupervised Robot Modeling from Point Cloud Frames Using Cluster Registration
output: articulated asset (URDF/MJCF) — robot URDF
evaluation: Segmentation, topology and joint estimation accuracy on robots up to 18 DoF from synthetic and real point-cloud sequences.

generalization.note: The URDF can be driven by new motor commands, though evaluation centres on structure recovery.

summary: Builds a robot's URDF without supervision from time series of point clouds captured while the robot moves randomly.
how: Clusters points in the first frame, registers clusters across frames to get 6-DoF transforms, then infers part segmentation, kinematic tree and joints and exports meshes plus URDF.

lab_fit.note: Observation-only and outputs a drivable kinematic model whose response to unseen commands can be scored.

name: DIPO
title: DIPO: Dual-State Images Controlled Articulated Object Generation Powered by Diverse Data
output: articulated asset (URDF/MJCF)
evaluation: Structure, joint and geometry metrics on PartNet-Mobility and the new PM-X dataset compared with SINGAPO and URDFormer-style baselines.

generalization.note: Evaluation is generation fidelity only.

summary: Generates articulated objects from a pair of images showing the resting and articulated states, using the second state as motion cue.
how: A dual-image diffusion model predicts part layout and joints, a chain-of-thought graph reasoner infers part connectivity, and training uses the LEGO-Art-expanded PM-X dataset.

lab_fit.note: Two-state image input fits an observation platform, but parts are retrieved rather than fitted to the instance.

name: FreeArt3D
title: FreeArt3D: Training-Free Articulated Object Generation using 3D Diffusion
output: articulated asset (URDF/MJCF) — textured part meshes + joints
evaluation: Geometry, appearance and joint accuracy on PartNet-Mobility versus learned articulated-generation baselines, plus real captured images.

generalization.note: No test of the generated asset under unseen interactions.

summary: Training-free method that turns a few images of an object at different articulation states into a textured articulated asset in minutes.
how: Uses a pretrained static 3D diffusion model (e.g. Trellis) as prior and extends score distillation to articulation, jointly optimizing part geometry and joint parameters per instance.

lab_fit.note: Per-instance fitting from multi-state images with explicit joints suits hidden-state prediction.

name: iTACO (Video2Articulation)
title: iTACO: Interactable Digital Twins of Articulated Objects from Casually Captured RGBD Videos
output: articulated asset (URDF/MJCF)
evaluation: Joint estimation and part geometry errors on 784 synthetic videos of 284 PartNet-Mobility objects and on real casually captured videos.

generalization.note: Evaluation is reconstruction accuracy only.

summary: Recovers interactable articulated twins from hand-held RGB-D videos of a person manipulating an object, despite camera motion and occlusion.
how: A coarse stage estimates joint parameters and movable-part segmentation from the video; a gradient-based refinement fits them to a reconstructed surface point cloud.

lab_fit.note: Takes casual interaction videos, a natural observation format, and outputs explicit joints.

name: Kinematify
title: Kinematify: Open-Vocabulary Synthesis of High-DoF Articulated Objects
output: articulated asset (URDF/MJCF)
evaluation: Kinematic-tree and joint-parameter accuracy on high-DoF objects (robots, animals, mechanisms) against prior articulated-object methods.

generalization.note: Joints are inferred from static geometry and not tested against observed motion.

summary: Synthesizes high-DoF articulated models such as humanoids and quadrupeds from an image or text without any motion data.
how: Generates a 3D mesh, searches the kinematic tree with MCTS under structural regularity objectives, and estimates revolute/prismatic joints from static geometry (DW-CAVL) before exporting URDF.

lab_fit.note: Does not use observed dynamics, so it cannot fit behaviour to the given observations.

name: PhysX-Anything
title: PhysX-Anything: Simulation-Ready Physical 3D Assets from Single Image
output: articulated asset (URDF/MJCF) — with physical attributes
evaluation: Geometric and physical-attribute metrics on the PhysX-Mobility dataset plus in-the-wild images, and contact-rich policy learning in MuJoCo.

generalization.note: Assets are used for new robot tasks in sim but not compared to the real object's behaviour.

summary: VLM-based generator that outputs a simulation-ready articulated asset with geometry, joints and physical properties from one in-the-wild image.
how: A VLM produces coarse geometry and physical/kinematic tokens; a controllable flow transformer refines geometry, and the result is exported as URDF/XML.

lab_fit.note: Easy to run; physical properties are priors from a single image, not fitted to observed dynamics.

name: Real2Code
title: Real2Code: Reconstruct Articulated Objects via Code Generation
output: articulated asset (URDF/MJCF) — MJCF code
evaluation: Geometry and joint-prediction accuracy on PartNet-Mobility objects with up to 10 parts versus PARIS and Ditto, plus real-world reconstructions.

generalization.note: Scores the reconstructed structure, not behaviour under new interactions.

summary: Reconstructs multi-part articulated objects by having a fine-tuned code LLM write their simulator code from oriented part bounding boxes.
how: DUSt3R and a part segmenter recover oriented bounding boxes per part; a fine-tuned CodeLlama predicts joints as executable MJCF code.

lab_fit.note: Already emits executable simulator code from a few images, matching a re-runnable-simulation contract.

name: Scalable Real2Sim
title: Scalable Real2Sim: Physics-Aware Asset Generation Via Robotic Pick-and-Place Setups
output: object mesh + physical properties — visual/collision geometry + inertial parameters
evaluation: Accuracy of reconstructed geometry and identified inertial parameters against ground truth, and fidelity of simulated object behaviour.

generalization.note: Identified inertia supports new manipulations in sim, but held-out real interactions are only lightly tested.

summary: Fully automated pick-and-place cell that scans objects and identifies collision geometry and inertial parameters to produce simulation-ready rigid assets.
how: The robot regrasps each object for a camera to reconstruct visual and collision meshes, then executes excitation trajectories and fits mass, center of mass and inertia from joint torques.

lab_fit.note: Needs a physical robot to collect interaction data; not runnable from fixed observations.

name: SINGAPO
title: SINGAPO: Single Image Controlled Generation of Articulated Parts in Objects
output: articulated asset (URDF/MJCF)
evaluation: Realism, image resemblance and reconstruction metrics against URDFormer and an image-conditioned NAP.

generalization.note: No test of generated objects under new interactions.

summary: Generates an articulated object consistent with a single resting-state image using a graph-conditioned diffusion model.
how: GPT-4o infers the part connectivity graph; a DDPM transformer conditioned on DINOv2 features generates part boxes and joints; part meshes are retrieved from a library.

lab_fit.note: Single-image generation favours plausibility over faithfulness to the observed instance's dynamics.

name: URDF-Anything
title: URDF-Anything: Constructing Articulated Objects with 3D Multimodal Language Model
output: articulated asset (URDF/MJCF)
evaluation: Segmentation mIoU, kinematic parameter error and physical executability of URDFs on PartNet-Mobility, including out-of-distribution objects.

generalization.note: Measures structure and executability, not behaviour under new interactions.

summary: End-to-end 3D multimodal LLM that segments parts and predicts joints from a point cloud to emit an executable URDF.
how: An autoregressive 3D MLLM reads point-cloud and text tokens; a [SEG] token queries point features for part masks while the model outputs kinematic parameters.

lab_fit.note: Requires a reconstructed point cloud first; outputs simulator-ready URDF.

name: ArtiTwinSplat
title: ArtiTwinSplat: Interactable Digital Twin Reconstruction via Gaussian Splatting from RGB-D videos
output: articulated asset (URDF/MJCF) — Gaussian-splat parts + joint kinematics
evaluation: Rendering quality and joint/part recovery on real-world RGB-D videos of articulated objects.

generalization.note: Twins can be manipulated interactively to new states, but not scored against held-out real motions.

summary: Unsupervised pipeline that builds photorealistic, interactable articulated Gaussian-splat twins from RGB-D videos without CAD or annotations.
how: Tracks motion in the RGB-D video to infer part structure and joint kinematics, then optimizes a part-wise 3D Gaussian Splatting model for real-time rendering and manipulation.

lab_fit.note: Video in, drivable twin out; directly comparable on hidden articulation queries.

name: URDF-Anything+
title: URDF-Anything+: End-to-End Generation for Simulation-Ready Articulated Assets
output: articulated asset (URDF/MJCF)
evaluation: Geometry, joint estimation and physical executability versus multi-stage pipelines, plus zero-shot transfer of sim-trained manipulation policies.

generalization.note: Policies trained on generated URDFs transfer to real objects; twin fidelity under new interactions is not directly scored.

summary: Autoregressive diffusion model that generates simulation-ready URDFs part by part directly from a single RGB image.
how: Each step generates one link's geometry and its joint parameters conditioned on the image and previous parts; a termination token decides the number of parts.

lab_fit.note: Fast single-image baseline; faithfulness to the specific observed instance is limited.

name: Phone2Proc
title: Phone2Proc: Bringing Robust Robots Into Our Chaotic World
output: digital cousin scenes — procedurally generated variants of a scanned room
evaluation: Real-world object-navigation success over 200+ trials in homes and offices, including robustness to lighting, clutter and people.

generalization.note: Agents are tested in the real environment under changes not present in the scan.

summary: Uses a 10-minute phone scan to procedurally generate many layout-consistent simulated variants of a real environment for robust navigation training.
how: An iPhone RoomPlan scan provides room and large-object layout; conditional ProcTHOR generation randomizes objects, materials and lighting around it.

lab_fit.note: Generates scene distributions, not a faithful predictive twin.

name: ACDC
title: Automated Creation of Digital Cousins for Robust Policy Learning
output: digital cousin scenes
evaluation: Scene reconstruction similarity and zero-shot sim-to-real policy success (90% for cousins vs 25% for twins).

generalization.note: Policies trained on cousin scenes are evaluated zero-shot in the real scene.

summary: Automatically builds many semantically and geometrically similar simulated 'digital cousin' scenes from one real RGB image to train robust policies.
how: Extracts objects with foundation models, matches each to articulated BEHAVIOR-1K assets by DINOv2 feature distance, and composes and post-processes them into OmniGibson scenes.

lab_fit.note: Deliberately produces approximate cousins rather than a faithful predictive twin.

name: CASHER
title: Robot Learning with Super-Linear Scaling
output: policy — trained across crowdsourced scene twins
evaluation: Zero-shot and few-shot real-world success on three manipulation tasks as the number of crowdsourced scenes grows.

generalization.note: Generalist policies are tested in unseen real scenes.

summary: Crowdsources smartphone-scanned digital twins and amortizes human demos with RL so data and performance scale super-linearly with human effort.
how: Non-experts scan scenes with phones to create sim twins; RL bootstrapped with a few demos generates data, a generalist policy is distilled and can be fine-tuned to a new scene from a scan.

lab_fit.note: Aimed at policy scaling, not at a re-runnable predictive simulation of a given observation.

name: RialTo
title: Reconciling Reality through Simulation: A Real-to-Sim-to-Real Approach for Robust Manipulation
output: policy — trained in an articulated digital twin of the target scene
evaluation: Real-world success and robustness to disturbances and distractors on eight manipulation tasks versus imitation-learning baselines.

generalization.note: Policies trained in the twin are tested in the real scene under perturbations, distractors and new poses.

summary: Builds a digital twin of a real scene with a GUI and uses RL in it to robustify imitation policies before real deployment.
how: A phone scan is turned into an articulated sim scene with a lightweight GUI; real demos are transferred via inverse distillation and the policy is fine-tuned with RL, then distilled back to real.

lab_fit.note: Twin construction is human-in-the-loop and the goal is a policy, not a predictive simulation.

name: Robo-GS
title: Robo-GS: A Physics Consistent Spatial-Temporal Model for Robotic Arm with Hybrid Representation
output: Gaussian-splat simulator scene — robot arm + scene hybrid mesh/Gaussian asset
evaluation: Rendering quality of robot arm and scene under motion versus 4DGS-style baselines on CR3, CR5 and UR5 arms.

generalization.note: The arm can be driven by new joint commands in sim with consistent rendering, but physical fidelity is not measured.

summary: Real2Sim pipeline that binds Gaussian splats to robot-arm meshes and physics attributes for consistent rendering and collision in simulation.
how: Gaussian-Mesh-Pixel binding maps mesh vertices to Gaussians, and ODE-based deformation replaces MLP deformation fields so the arm moves consistently in both sim and splat views.

lab_fit.note: Focuses on robot appearance rather than predicting object dynamics.

name: RoboGSim
title: RoboGSim: A Real2Sim2Real Robotic Gaussian Splatting Simulator
output: Gaussian-splat simulator scene
evaluation: Rendering fidelity of synthesized demos and zero-shot real-robot performance of policies trained on its data; closed-loop policy evaluation in sim.

generalization.note: Policies trained or evaluated in the GS sim are compared with real-robot rollouts.

summary: Gaussian-splatting simulator that rebuilds real scenes and objects, composes new layouts and serves both as data synthesizer and closed-loop policy evaluator.
how: A Gaussian reconstructor and digital-twin builder align 3DGS with Isaac Sim meshes; a scene composer edits layouts and an interactive engine renders physics-driven rollouts.

lab_fit.note: Re-runnable sim with a closed-loop evaluator; physics parameters are not fitted.

name: SplatSim
title: SplatSim: Zero-Shot Sim2Real Transfer of RGB Manipulation Policies Using Gaussian Splatting
output: Gaussian-splat simulator scene
evaluation: Real-world success of RGB policies trained only on SplatSim data (86.25% avg) versus real-data policies (97.5%) on four tasks.

generalization.note: Policies trained purely in the splat-rendered sim are deployed zero-shot on the real robot.

summary: Replaces mesh rendering in an existing simulator with Gaussian splats of the real scene and robot to train RGB policies that transfer zero-shot.
how: Segments splats of the robot and objects, attaches them to simulator links and rigid bodies, and re-renders them with the simulated poses at every step.

lab_fit.note: Gives a re-runnable photoreal sim, but physical parameters are not identified from observations.

name: DISCOVERSE
title: DISCOVERSE: Efficient Robot Simulation in Complex High-Fidelity Environments
output: Gaussian-splat simulator scene
evaluation: Rendering speed and zero-shot sim-to-real success of ACT and Diffusion Policy trained on its data, with image-augmentation ablations.

generalization.note: Policies trained in reconstructed scenes are deployed on real robots.

summary: Open-source modular 3DGS + MuJoCo simulator with a real2sim pipeline for building high-fidelity robot learning environments.
how: Real captures, generated content and existing assets are converted to 3DGS, mesh and MJCF; Gaussian rendering is coupled to MuJoCo physics with ROS2 interfaces and parallel simulation.

lab_fit.note: MuJoCo-based re-runnable scenes; physical parameters are set manually.

name: DRAWER
title: DRAWER: Digital Reconstruction and Articulation With Environment Realism
output: simulation-ready scene — interactable articulated room
evaluation: Reconstruction/rendering quality, articulation accuracy, an Unreal Engine game demo and real-to-sim-to-real robot manipulation.

generalization.note: Articulated drawers/doors can be opened in sim and used for real-to-sim-to-real, but behaviour is not scored against held-out real interactions.

summary: Converts a video of a static indoor scene into a photorealistic, interactable virtual environment with articulated drawers and doors.
how: A dual Gaussian/SDF scene representation is paired with an articulation module that detects openable parts, infers hinges and joint types, and completes interiors for simulation.

lab_fit.note: Video in, articulated scene out; articulation is inferred from priors since no motion is observed.

name: DreMa
title: Dream to Manipulate: Compositional World Models Empowering Robot Imitation Learning with Imagination
output: Gaussian-splat simulator scene — object-centric compositional world model
evaluation: Imitation-learning success in simulation and on a real Franka with data imagined by equivariant transformations of a few demos.

generalization.note: Imagined novel configurations are used to train policies that succeed on unseen real task variations.

summary: Builds an object-centric Gaussian-splat twin embedded in a physics engine to imagine new demonstrations for one-shot imitation learning.
how: Segments the scene into object-wise Gaussians with meshes, places them in PyBullet, and applies equivariant transformations to demos, verifying them by simulated rollout.

lab_fit.note: Yields a re-runnable compositional sim from observations; physics parameters are defaults.

name: GaussGym
title: GaussGym: An open-source real-to-sim framework for learning locomotion from pixels
output: Gaussian-splat simulator scene — for visual locomotion
evaluation: Simulation throughput, visual-policy behaviour in reconstructed scenes and partial real-world transfer of RGB locomotion policies.

generalization.note: Policies are tested in real scenes, with acknowledged drops in unseen environments.

summary: Fast open-source simulator that combines 3D Gaussian splatting of real scenes with vectorized physics to train locomotion from RGB pixels.
how: Reconstructs scenes from phone scans, robot logs or generated videos into aligned splats plus meshes, and renders them in batch alongside IsaacGym physics at over 100k steps/s.

lab_fit.note: Built for policy training at scale, not for predicting a specific observed physical outcome.

name: GSWorld
title: GSWorld: Closed-Loop Photo-Realistic Simulation Suite for Robotic Manipulation
output: Gaussian-splat simulator scene
evaluation: Closed-loop policy evaluation correlation with real-world results, zero-shot sim-to-real policy learning and visual RL.

generalization.note: Sim policy evaluations and trained policies are compared against real-robot outcomes.

summary: Photoreal closed-loop simulation suite that reconstructs metric-scale Gaussian-splat twins of real workspaces aligned with robot URDFs.
how: Short multi-view captures produce metric 3DGS scenes and object assets; the robot URDF is aligned and the splats are rendered alongside a physics engine for training and evaluation.

lab_fit.note: Re-runnable twin designed for policy evaluation; dynamics are not identified from observations.

name: Human2Sim2Robot
title: Crossing the Human-Robot Embodiment Gap with Sim-to-Real RL using One Human Demonstration
output: policy — dexterous RL in a real-to-sim scene from one human demo
evaluation: Zero-shot real success on a Kuka-Allegro across grasping, non-prehensile and multi-step tasks versus replay and imitation baselines.

generalization.note: Policies are trained with randomization in sim and tested on the real robot under new object poses.

summary: Trains dexterous manipulation policies by reconstructing the scene from one human RGB-D video and running sim RL with an object-pose reward.
how: The object pose trajectory from the video defines an embodiment-agnostic reward and the pre-grasp hand pose initializes exploration; RL in the reconstructed sim transfers zero-shot.

lab_fit.note: Policy-learning focus; the scene twin is not evaluated as a predictor.

name: MetaScenes
title: MetaScenes: Towards Automated Replica Creation for Real-world 3D Scans
output: simulation-ready scene — asset-replaced replicas of real scans
evaluation: Asset-retrieval quality, small-object layout synthesis for manipulation and VLN sim-to-real domain transfer.

generalization.note: Replicas are used to train agents that are tested across domains, not checked against new physical interactions.

summary: Scan2Sim model and dataset that turn real-world 3D scans into simulatable replica scenes by automatically replacing objects with physics-ready assets.
how: A multi-modal alignment model matches each scanned object to an asset, which is placed and physically validated to build 15k-object simulatable scenes.

lab_fit.note: Scene-level asset replacement; no dynamics fitted to observations.

name: Re3Sim
title: Re$^3$Sim: Generating High-Fidelity Simulation Data via 3D-Photorealistic Real-to-Sim for Robotic Manipulation
output: Gaussian-splat simulator scene
evaluation: Zero-shot sim-to-real success of policies trained only on generated data (above 58% on average) and sim-real visual alignment.

generalization.note: Policies trained in the reconstructed scene are evaluated on the real robot.

summary: Reconstructs real tabletop scenes as meshes plus Gaussian splats in Isaac Sim to generate photorealistic expert demonstrations for imitation learning.
how: Recovers scene/object meshes for physics and 3DGS for rendering, composites foreground and background views, and runs privileged planners to collect large demo sets.

lab_fit.note: Produces a re-runnable sim scene; dynamics use default rigid parameters rather than fitted ones.

name: Real-is-Sim
title: Real-is-Sim: Bridging the Sim-to-Real Gap with a Dynamic Digital Twin
output: simulation-ready scene — continuously synchronized dynamic digital twin
evaluation: Correlation between virtual and real-world PushT success rates, plus policies trained on augmented virtual rollouts.

generalization.note: Virtual policy evaluations are checked against real-world outcomes for new policies.

summary: Puts a real-time-corrected Embodied-Gaussians digital twin inside the behaviour-cloning loop so policies act on the sim and the real robot follows.
how: The twin is synchronized with real cameras at 60 Hz via visual correction forces; policies observe and act in the twin, enabling offline evaluation and data augmentation.

lab_fit.note: Twin is meant to track reality with corrections; open-loop prediction under hidden conditions is not its focus.

name: Real2Render2Real (R2R2R)
title: Real2Render2Real: Scaling Robot Data Without Dynamics Simulation or Robot Hardware
output: Gaussian-splat simulator scene — kinematic rendering of object trajectories, no dynamics
evaluation: Real-robot success of VLA/diffusion policies trained on R2R2R data versus 150 teleoperated demos, across 1,050 physical trials.

generalization.note: Generated trajectories vary object poses for policy training; no physics is simulated, so unseen dynamics cannot be predicted.

summary: Generates robot training data from a phone scan and one human video by rendering object and robot trajectories without dynamics simulation.
how: Reconstructs objects as Gaussian splats, tracks 6-DoF part motion from the human video, synthesizes varied object trajectories and robot IK motions, and renders them in Isaac Lab.

lab_fit.note: Kinematic replay only; no physics to roll out under hidden conditions.

name: ReBot
title: ReBot: Scaling Robot Learning with Real-to-Sim-to-Real Robotic Video Synthesis
output: policy — training videos synthesized by sim replay over inpainted real backgrounds
evaluation: Octo and OpenVLA success in SimplerEnv (WidowX) and on a real Franka after training on synthesized videos.

generalization.note: Augmented data improves out-of-domain policy success, but the sim replay itself is not checked for physical fidelity.

summary: Replays real robot trajectories in simulation with new objects and composites them onto inpainted real backgrounds to scale VLA training data.
how: Real episodes are replayed in sim to swap manipulated objects, the real background is inpainted, and sim foreground is composited back into realistic videos.

lab_fit.note: Data augmentation tool, not a predictive simulation builder.

name: RoboSimGS
title: High-Fidelity Simulated Data Generation for Real-World Zero-Shot Robotic Manipulation Learning with Gaussian Splatting
output: Gaussian-splat simulator scene — with MLLM-inferred physical properties
evaluation: Zero-shot real-world manipulation success of policies trained only on generated data, and gains when augmenting real data.

generalization.note: Policies trained purely in the reconstructed sim are deployed zero-shot on real tasks.

summary: Real2Sim2Real framework that builds interactive simulation scenes from multi-view images using Gaussian splats for appearance and mesh primitives for physics.
how: Reconstructs scenes with 3DGS, represents interactive objects as meshes, and uses a multimodal LLM to infer physical properties and articulation before generating training data.

lab_fit.note: Assigns physical properties from priors, giving a re-runnable but not dynamics-fitted twin.

name: Vid2Sim
title: Vid2Sim: Realistic and Interactive Simulation from Video for Urban Navigation
output: Gaussian-splat simulator scene — for urban navigation
evaluation: Navigation success of agents trained in reconstructed environments, in digital twins (+31.2%) and the real world (+68.3%).

generalization.note: Agents trained in video-built sims are evaluated in real-world navigation.

summary: Converts a monocular web or hand-held video into an interactive Gaussian-splat plus mesh simulation for training urban navigation agents.
how: Geometry-consistent Gaussian splatting with mesh primitives reconstructs the scene, which is exported with collision meshes into Unity for RL with added obstacles and agents.

lab_fit.note: Navigation-focused environments; little object dynamics to predict.

name: VR-Robo
title: VR-Robo: A Real-to-Sim-to-Real Framework for Visual Robot Navigation and Locomotion
output: Gaussian-splat simulator scene — for legged robots
evaluation: Zero-shot real-world success of RGB-only visual goal-tracking policies for a quadruped trained in the reconstructed twin.

generalization.note: Policies trained in the reconstructed scene are deployed on the real robot.

summary: Builds photorealistic GS-plus-mesh digital twins of real environments so legged robots can learn RGB-only navigation and locomotion with zero-shot transfer.
how: Reconstructs scenes with 3DGS and aligned meshes, imports them into Isaac Sim for physics, renders ego-centric RGB from splats and trains RL policies.

lab_fit.note: Environment reconstruction for locomotion, not object-level physical prediction.

name: X-Sim
title: X-Sim: Cross-Embodiment Learning via Real-to-Sim-to-Real
output: policy — RL in photorealistic reconstruction driven by object motion from human video
evaluation: Real-robot task progress on 5 manipulation tasks in 2 environments versus hand-tracking and sim-to-real baselines (~30% improvement).

generalization.note: Policies learned in the reconstructed sim are deployed on a real robot with a different embodiment from the human demonstrator.

summary: Learns robot policies from human videos by reconstructing the scene in simulation and using tracked object motion as the reward signal.
how: Phone scan and RGB-D video give a photorealistic ManiSkill scene and object trajectories; RL learns to reproduce them, then distills into an image diffusion policy with online domain adaptation.

lab_fit.note: Uses real2sim only as a policy-learning substrate.

name: ExoGS
title: ExoGS: A 4D Real-to-Sim-to-Real Framework for Scalable Manipulation Data Collection
output: Gaussian-splat simulator scene — editable 4D robot/object/scene assets
evaluation: Real-world data efficiency and policy generalization under visual domain shifts versus teleoperation-collected data.

generalization.note: Augmented replays improve policies under visual shifts; interaction dynamics are replayed, not re-simulated.

summary: Robot-free real-to-sim-to-real framework that records human demos with a passive exoskeleton and rebuilds them as editable Gaussian-splat assets for augmentation.
how: The AirExo-3 exoskeleton logs robot-consistent trajectories with synced RGB; robot, objects and scene become 3DGS assets that are replayed and edited, with a Mask Adapter for policy robustness.

lab_fit.note: Replay-based data engine without forward physics prediction.

name: Mind's Eye
title: Mind's Eye: Grounded Language Model Reasoning through Simulation
output: MuJoCo simulation code generated per question; outcomes injected into the LM prompt
evaluation: Accuracy on 39 tasks of a physics alignment benchmark (UTOPIA), zero-shot and few-shot.

generalization.note: Simulation is run per question; no reusable program is tested.

summary: Grounds LM physical reasoning by translating a question into simulation code, running MuJoCo, and feeding outcomes back as context.
how: A text-to-code LM writes MuJoCo rendering code for the question; simulated results are appended to the prompt of a foundation LM.

lab_fit.note: Uses simulation as a reasoning tool rather than delivering a reconstructed simulator.

name: 3D-GPT
title: 3D-GPT: Procedural 3D Modeling with Large Language Models
output: Blender / Infinigen procedural modeling calls
evaluation: Qualitative results and alignment of generated scenes to instructions, plus multi-turn editing demos.

generalization.note: No held-out conditions; scenes are assessed against their text instructions.

summary: Three LLM agents translate text into parameters for procedural generators, producing 3D scenes in Blender.
how: Task-dispatch, conceptualization and modeling agents enrich the description and select and parameterize procedural generation functions.

lab_fit.note: Static text-to-3D procedural modeling, no physics or observations.

name: Eureka
title: Eureka: Human-Level Reward Design via Coding Large Language Models
output: reward code
evaluation: Policy performance with Eureka rewards vs. expert human rewards on 29 RL environments with 10 robot morphologies.

generalization.note: Reward programs are evaluated by training on the same environment they were written for.

summary: GPT-4 writes reward functions from environment source code and evolves them with RL training feedback, beating human-designed rewards.
how: Samples many reward programs, trains policies, summarizes training statistics as reflection, and iteratively mutates the best program.

lab_fit.note: Generates reward code for a given simulator rather than the simulator itself.

name: Gen2Sim
title: Gen2Sim: Scaling up Robot Learning in Simulation with Generative Models
output: URDF assets with LLM-estimated physics, task decompositions and Python reward functions
evaluation: Success of RL policies on generated long-horizon tasks with vs. without temporal task decomposition.

generalization.note: Generated assets and rewards are only used to learn the generated tasks.

summary: Lifts object images to 3D assets, asks LLMs for physical parameters, and prompts LLMs to write task decompositions and reward code.
how: Image diffusion lifts 2D images to meshes; LLMs fill physics parameters and chain-of-thought prompts produce tasks, sub-goals and reward functions for RL.

lab_fit.note: LLM-filled parameters are a minor real2sim step; overall it is environment generation.

name: GenSim
title: GenSim: Generating Robotic Simulation Tasks via Large Language Models
output: PyBullet task code (Ravens/CLIPort-style tasks)
evaluation: Code-generation success of LLMs on simulation tasks and task-level generalization of multitask policies in sim and real.

generalization.note: Generated tasks are tested by training policies that must generalize to unseen tasks, not the programs themselves.

summary: GPT-4 proposes and writes new robotic simulation tasks with demonstrations, expanding a benchmark tenfold for multitask policy training.
how: Goal-directed and exploratory modes prompt an LLM with a task library; generated code is checked by execution and demonstration success before being added.

lab_fit.note: Code generation of tasks from text; no real observations, so it fits as an environment generator rather than a real2sim method.

name: GPT4Motion
title: GPT4Motion: Scripting Physical Motions in Text-to-Video Generation via Blender-Oriented GPT Planning
output: Blender physics simulation script
evaluation: Motion coherency and text alignment of generated videos for rigid drop/collision, cloth and liquid scenarios vs. text-to-video baselines.

generalization.note: Each script is rendered once for its prompt.

summary: GPT-4 writes Blender scripts that run built-in physics to produce coherent motion, which then conditions a diffusion model for video.
how: Outputs of the generated Blender physics simulation are fed to Stable Diffusion as conditioning to render the final frames.

lab_fit.note: Text-to-physics-script generation; a natural baseline for code-based physical video, though not from observations.

name: Holodeck
title: Holodeck: Language Guided Generation of 3D Embodied AI Environments
output: AI2-THOR scene (layout, objects, constraints)
evaluation: Large-scale human preference studies vs. procedural baselines, and navigation agents trained in generated scenes.

generalization.note: Scenes are judged as generated; no held-out conditions.

summary: GPT-4 designs 3D embodied-AI environments from text, placing Objaverse assets by solving LLM-written spatial constraints.
how: The LLM proposes floor plans, materials, objects and relational constraints; a constraint solver optimizes the final layout.

lab_fit.note: Text-to-scene generation for embodied AI, not reconstruction from observations.

name: RoboGen
title: RoboGen: Towards Unleashing Infinite Data for Automated Robot Learning via Generative Simulation
output: generated scenes, task decompositions and reward/training code
evaluation: Diversity of generated tasks and success of skills learned via RL, motion planning or trajectory optimization.

generalization.note: Each generated environment is used to learn its own skill; no held-out tests of the scene program.

summary: A propose-generate-learn agent uses foundation models to invent tasks, build simulation scenes, and generate supervision for skill learning.
how: An LLM proposes tasks, populates scenes from asset libraries with spatial configurations, decomposes tasks, picks a learning method, and writes rewards.

lab_fit.note: Environment generation without observations; not a real-to-sim method.

name: SimLM
title: SimLM: Can Language Models Infer Parameters of Physical Systems?
output: inferred physical parameters checked by a simulator
evaluation: Accuracy of LLM-inferred parameters for a simple physical system with and without simulator access.

generalization.note: Tested on the same simple system used for inference.

summary: Shows LLMs struggle at inferring physical-system parameters and that adding simulator feedback to the context helps.
