how: LLMs propose parameters, a physics simulator returns outcomes, and these are fed back in context for refinement.

lab_fit.note: Early probe of simulator-in-the-loop parameter inference; too small to be a platform method.

name: Text2Reward
title: Text2Reward: Reward Shaping with Language Models for Reinforcement Learning
output: dense reward code
evaluation: Success rate and convergence of RL policies with generated vs. expert rewards on 17 manipulation tasks and MuJoCo locomotion, plus real-robot deployment.

generalization.note: Rewards are tested only on the tasks they were written for.

summary: An LLM writes shaped dense reward programs from a goal description and a compact environment abstraction, refinable with human feedback.
how: A Pythonic environment abstraction is given to the LLM, which outputs reward code; optional human feedback after rollouts drives refinement.

lab_fit.note: Reward-code generation, not simulation building.

name: GenSim2
title: GenSim2: Scaling Robot Data Generation with Multi-modal and Reasoning LLMs
output: articulated-object task code with solvers and demonstrations
evaluation: Number and success of generated long-horizon articulated tasks, and sim-to-real zero-shot transfer / co-training of a multi-task policy.

generalization.note: Policies trained on generated tasks are tested in the real world; programs are not tested under hidden conditions.

summary: Multimodal and reasoning LLMs generate complex articulated manipulation tasks and solvers to mass-produce demonstrations.
how: LLMs write task code, planning and RL solvers produce demos, and a proprioceptive point-cloud transformer policy learns from them.

lab_fit.note: Program generation from text/assets; relevant for environment synthesis rather than reconstruction.

name: GIF-MCTS
title: Generating Code World Models with Large Language Models Guided by Monte Carlo Tree Search
output: Python code world model
evaluation: Prediction accuracy of synthesized code world models on the Code World Models Benchmark (18 RL environments) and planning returns.

generalization.note: Models are checked on held-out transitions and used for planning beyond the provided trajectories.

summary: Synthesizes Python world models from environment descriptions and trajectories using MCTS over generate, improve and fix actions.
how: An LLM-guided tree search proposes, refines and debugs code using unit tests and trajectory mismatches; the best program becomes the planner's model.

lab_fit.note: Close in spirit (program fitted to data, tested on held-out transitions) but inputs are states, not video.

name: IG-LLM
title: Re-Thinking Inverse Graphics With Large Language Models
institution: Max Planck Institute for Intelligent Systems
output: structured compositional 3D scene representation (code-like)
evaluation: Accuracy of recovered object attributes and poses on CLEVR-style and other synthetic scenes, including out-of-distribution compositions.

generalization.note: Tests compositional generalization to attribute combinations held out from training.

summary: A fine-tuned LLM decodes a visual embedding into a structured 3D scene description that re-renders the input image.
how: A frozen visual encoder feeds an LLM that autoregressively emits a scene program, with a continuous numeric head for precise parameters; trained end-to-end without image-space supervision.

lab_fit.note: A trained single-pass model for static scenes, not an agent that iterates in a sandbox.

name: LLMPhy
title: LLMPhy: Parameter-Identifiable Physical Reasoning Combining Large Language Models and Physics Engines
output: Python programs setting MuJoCo physical parameters and scene layout (digital twin)
evaluation: Zero-shot physical reasoning on three new datasets (e.g. TraySim): accuracy of predicted outcomes and recovered physical parameters vs. Bayesian optimization, CMA-ES and LLM-only baselines.

generalization.note: Parameters identified from observed trials are used to simulate and predict outcomes of a new, unseen impact on the scene.

summary: An LLM writes code proposing friction, damping and layout, runs it in MuJoCo, and refines from reconstruction error to build a digital twin for reasoning.
how: Two phases (continuous parameters, discrete layout); each iterates LLM-generated programs, executes them in the physics engine, and feeds the reconstruction error back to the LLM.

lab_fit.note: Observation-in, program-out loop with simulator feedback; the identified twin can be frozen and re-run on held-out interventions.

name: NeRF2Physics
title: Physical Property Understanding from Language-Embedded Feature Fields
output: dense per-point physical properties (mass density, friction, hardness)
evaluation: Error in estimated object mass and other properties (friction, hardness) on real objects.

generalization.note: Properties are evaluated directly against measured values, not by running a simulation under new conditions.

summary: An LLM proposes candidate materials per object; a language-embedded point cloud maps them to dense physical properties for simulation.
how: Multi-view images build a CLIP-embedded point cloud; LLM-suggested materials and value ranges are assigned by zero-shot kernel regression.

lab_fit.note: Produces physical parameters rather than a program; useful as a component of an agent, not as a standalone method.

name: OMNI-EPIC
title: OMNI-EPIC: Open-endedness via Models of human Notions of Interestingness with Environments Programmed in Code
output: environment and reward code
evaluation: Qualitative open-ended task archives and RL agent learning progress over generated environments.

generalization.note: Environments are generated for continual learning, not tested as models of observed systems.

summary: Foundation models continuously write code for new learnable, interesting environments and rewards to drive open-ended RL.
how: An archive of tasks conditions an LLM to propose and code the next task; a model of interestingness filters it and success detectors judge completion.

lab_fit.note: Open-ended environment generation, no real observations.

name: SceneCraft
title: SceneCraft: An LLM Agent for Synthesizing 3D Scene as Blender Code
output: Blender Python scene script
evaluation: Constraint adherence, CLIP score and human evaluation vs. LLM-agent baselines (e.g. BlenderGPT); demo reconstructions of Sintel movie scenes.

generalization.note: Scenes are judged against their own descriptions.

summary: An LLM agent turns text into Blender scripts via a scene-graph blueprint, refines with GPT-V feedback on renders, and learns a reusable function library.
how: Plans a scene graph, converts relations into numeric layout constraints in code, critiques renders with a VLM, and accumulates skills across tasks.

lab_fit.note: Iterative code-render-critique loop transferable to observation-driven tasks, but static and text-driven.

name: WorldCoder
title: WorldCoder, a Model-Based LLM Agent: Building World Models by Writing Code and Interacting with the Environment
output: Python code world model (transition and reward)
evaluation: Sample and compute efficiency on gridworlds and task planning vs. deep RL and ReAct-style agents, and transfer across environments.

generalization.note: Learned code is transferred and edited for new environments and goals.

summary: An agent writes and debugs a Python world model from its own interactions, with an optimism constraint linking program and planner.
how: Program synthesis fits code to observed transitions; optimism under uncertainty drives exploration and planning with the learned program.

lab_fit.note: Learns a program from interaction data and tests it on new tasks, but in symbolic, non-physical domains.

name: PoE-World
title: PoE-World: Compositional World Modeling with Products of Programmatic Experts
output: product of LLM-synthesized programmatic experts (code world model)
evaluation: Planning performance and generalization to unseen levels on Atari Pong and Montezuma's Revenge from few observations.

generalization.note: Learned world models are used on unseen game levels.

summary: Represents a world model as a weighted product of many small LLM-written programs, learning complex stochastic dynamics from few observations.
how: LLMs synthesize many small rule programs; weights are fit to observed object-centric trajectories; the product model drives a planning agent.

lab_fit.note: Program world models validated on unseen conditions; game domains rather than real physics.

name: SIMPACT
title: SIMPACT: Simulation-Enabled Action Planning using Vision-Language Models
output: physics simulation of the observed scene used for VLM action planning
evaluation: Real-world success on five rigid and deformable manipulation tasks vs. general-purpose robot manipulation models.

generalization.note: The built simulator predicts outcomes of new candidate actions before execution.

summary: Builds a physics simulation from one RGB-D view so a VLM can propose actions, watch simulated rollouts, and refine its plan at test time.
how: Perception (segmentation, mesh generation, pose) instantiates a MuJoCo or MPM scene; the VLM iterates propose-simulate-reflect before acting.

lab_fit.note: Real-to-sim from a single observation with action-counterfactual rollouts; the sim is a planning tool rather than a delivered program.

name: Video2Policy
title: Video2Policy: Scaling up Manipulation Tasks in Simulation through Internet Videos
output: simulation task code and LLM-generated reward functions
evaluation: RL success on tasks reconstructed from 100+ Something-Something-v2 videos, generalist policy training, and Real2Sim2Real transfer.

generalization.note: Generated tasks are used to train policies that are tested on new task instances and a real robot, not the program itself.

summary: Reconstructs everyday human-video tasks as simulation code, then trains RL policies with iteratively refined LLM-generated rewards.
how: Objects and poses are extracted from internet videos to instantiate tasks in simulation via generated code; rewards are written and refined in-context by an LLM.

lab_fit.note: Video-to-sim-task code fits the platform, but evaluation centers on policy learning rather than program fidelity.

name: ChronoAgentic
title: ChronoAgentic: A Code-based Multi-Agent World Simulator for Physically Grounded Simulation Construction
output: executable PyChrono simulation program
evaluation: Semantic adherence and physical correctness on 80 PhyWorldBench demos vs. ten text-to-video models.

generalization.note: Programs are checked against their own plan; no hidden-condition reruns.

summary: Plan, code, visual-analysis and review agents build and repair PyChrono programs from prompts as a physically grounded alternative to video world models.
how: Code is grounded in a skill library, generative assets and simulator-source retrieval; rendered rollouts and deterministic physics checks drive iterative repair.

lab_fit.note: Agentic sim-code construction with physics checks; would need video inputs to serve as a real2sim method.

name: Code-as-World
title: Code as Worlds: Agentic Discovery of Executable World Representations for Physical Reasoning
output: executable world code (composition, dynamics, appearance)
evaluation: Verified executable worlds supply supervision for training a VLM (Code-as-World-VL), evaluated on the QuantiPhy quantitative physical reasoning benchmark.

generalization.note: Programs are verified against the source observation; generalization is shown mainly through the downstream VLM trained on them.

summary: An agent proposes, executes, renders, verifies and refines executable world hypotheses from text or real videos, then uses them as physical supervision.
how: An abductive discovery loop turns observations into MuJoCo code, renders it, compares with the observation, and converts discrepancies into structured feedback for code revision.

lab_fit.note: Directly a video-to-program agent loop; delivered world code could be frozen and re-executed under hidden interventions.

name: SEIG
title: Thinking in Blender: Staged Executable Inverse Graphics with Vision-Language Models
output: editable Blender program
evaluation: Single-image reconstruction fidelity measured with pixel-level, perceptual and semantic metrics across diverse scenes.

generalization.note: Evaluated only on reproducing the input image; no held-out conditions.

summary: A staged VLM agent reconstructs a single image as an editable Blender program, refining geometry, materials, composition and lighting in turn.
how: General-purpose VLMs edit Blender code stage by stage, rendering and comparing after each stage, without specialized 3D models or differentiable rendering.

lab_fit.note: Agentic image-to-Blender program; static scenes only, so hidden-condition tests would be relighting/viewpoint rather than physics.

name: Swim2Real
title: Swim2Real: Vision-Language Models for Simulator Calibration of a Soft Robotic Fish
output: calibrated 16-parameter soft-robot simulator
evaluation: Marker error over a fixed simulator budget vs. random and permuted directions, a preregistered replication, and hardware open-loop trials.

generalization.note: The calibrated simulator generates motor commands that are executed on hardware.

summary: A VLM compares real and simulated swimming videos to propose simulator parameter updates, accepted via backtracking line search.
how: VLM proposals give search directions over 16 parameters; a line search tests each and keeps updates that reduce tracked marker error.

lab_fit.note: Video-based calibration loop; parameter-level rather than program-level output.

name: Vid2Sid
title: Vid2Sid: Videos Can Help Close the Sim2Real Gap
output: calibrated simulator physics parameters with rationales
evaluation: Sim2real error on holdout controls for a tendon-actuated finger and a soft tentacle, plus sim2sim parameter recovery vs. black-box optimizers.

generalization.note: Calibrated simulators are evaluated on held-out control inputs unseen during calibration.

summary: A VLM compares paired real and simulated videos, diagnoses mismatches, and proposes interpretable physics parameter updates.
how: Foundation-model perception tracks the robot in video; a VLM-in-the-loop optimizer reads sim-real comparisons and outputs parameter updates with rationales.

lab_fit.note: Video-driven system ID with held-out controls matches a hidden-condition protocol; the agent edits parameters, not code.

name: VIGA
title: Vision-as-Inverse-Graphics Agent via Interleaved Multimodal Reasoning
output: Blender Python scene program
evaluation: Reconstruction/editing accuracy on BlenderGym, SlideBench and the new BlenderBench vs. one-shot VLM baselines.

generalization.note: Programs are scored against the same target images they were built from.

summary: A training-free VLM agent reconstructs images into editable Blender programs through a write-run-render-compare-revise loop.
how: Generation and verification roles alternate: code is executed and rendered, discrepancies with the target are inspected, and an evolving multimodal memory guides edits; also shown for 4D physical interaction.

lab_fit.note: Already a code-render-inspect agent; output is a standalone Blender program that can be re-run, though its evaluation is static.

name: VisualPatchWorld
title: VisualPatchWorld: Code World Models as Latent Structured Representations for Planning
output: Python code world model with fitted parameters
evaluation: Model-predictive-control planning success on navigation, grasping and pushing tasks vs. prior code world models and the ground-truth engine.

generalization.note: Induced programs are rolled out for planning from new states; image-derived scene graphs supply live state.

summary: Induces a Python dynamics program by choosing a qualitative physical form with active probes and fitting its parameters to state-action traces.
how: Short probes select the dynamical form; free parameters are fit by minimizing multi-step prediction error; the program is used inside MPC.

lab_fit.note: Structured program induction with held-out planning tests; inputs are traces, not raw video.

name: ΔYNAMICS
title: $Δ$ynamics: Language-Based Representation for Inferring Rigid-Body Dynamics From Videos
output: structured-text scene configuration for physics simulation
evaluation: Segmentation IoU of re-simulated motion on CLEVRER and a new set of 235 real-world rigid-body videos, compared with leading VLMs.

generalization.note: Transfers from synthetic training to real videos, but reproduction is scored on the observed clips.

summary: A vision-language model infers rigid-body states and properties from video as structured-text scene configs that a simulator replays.
how: Optical flow and language motion reasoning feed a VLM that emits simulator configurations; test-time sampling and evolutionary search refine them.

lab_fit.note: Outputs simulator configs (not free-form code) from video; configs could be frozen and re-simulated under changes.

name: DPI-Net
title: Learning Particle Dynamics for Manipulating Rigid Bodies, Deformable Objects, and Fluids
output: particle-based neural dynamics model for control
evaluation: Rollout position error versus FleX ground truth and success of model-based control, with online adaptation to a real robot task.

generalization.note: Shows online adaptation to unseen settings and a real-robot manipulation demo.

summary: Dynamic interaction networks over particles that learn multi-material dynamics and support model-based manipulation planning.
how: Hierarchical particle graphs with dynamic edges propagate effects in multi-step message passing; the model is differentiated through for control.

lab_fit.note: Delivered simulator is re-runnable, but trained from simulator states.

name: GNS
title: Learning to Simulate Complex Physics with Graph Networks
output: particle-based learned simulator (graph network)
evaluation: One-step and long-rollout particle position MSE against ground-truth simulators (SPH, MPM, PBD) on held-out initial conditions and larger domains.

generalization.note: Generalizes to more particles, longer rollouts and unseen obstacle configurations than in training.

summary: Graph-network simulator that learns particle dynamics for fluids, sand and goop, establishing the learned-simulator template.
how: Particles become graph nodes; an encode-process-decode GNN predicts accelerations, integrated forward to roll out trajectories.

lab_fit.note: Runnable learned simulator, but needs particle states rather than real visual observations.

name: RoboCraft
title: RoboCraft: Learning to See, Simulate, and Shape Elasto-Plastic Objects with Graph Networks
output: GNN particle dynamics model of real dough for model-based planning
evaluation: Prediction error (Chamfer/EMD) on held-out interactions and success of shaping real Play-Doh into target letters via MPC.

generalization.note: Model learned from ~10 minutes of real interaction plans for unseen target shapes and grip sequences.

summary: Learns a particle-based simulator of real elasto-plastic dough from RGB-D interaction data and uses it to plan shaping actions.
how: RGB-D point clouds are sampled into particles; a GNN learns gripper-dough dynamics, then MPC searches actions toward target shapes.

lab_fit.note: Real RGB-D observations in, re-runnable learned simulator out; scorable on held-out actions.

name: Dyn-Res
title: Dynamic-Resolution Model Learning for Object Pile Manipulation
output: resolution-adaptive GNN dynamics model of granular object piles
evaluation: Gathering, sorting and redistribution success on granular piles (coffee beans, almonds, corn) in simulation and the real world versus fixed-resolution baselines.

generalization.note: Adapts model resolution at test time and is evaluated on varied granular instances in simulation and the real world.

summary: Learns granular pile dynamics with a GNN whose abstraction level is selected adaptively at each MPC step for efficient manipulation.
how: Point clouds are downsampled to a learned resolution; a GNN predicts pushing dynamics and MPC optimizes actions toward target pile configurations.

lab_fit.note: Re-runnable learned dynamics with action conditioning; fits held-out rollout scoring.

name: RoboCook
title: RoboCook: Long-Horizon Elasto-Plastic Object Manipulation with Diverse Tools
output: tool-conditioned GNN dynamics models of real dough
evaluation: Dynamics prediction accuracy per tool and real-robot success on long-horizon dumpling/bun making, including robustness to perturbations.

generalization.note: Learned models drive multi-tool plans for unseen goal shapes with ~20 minutes of real data per tool.

summary: Learns per-tool GNN dynamics of real dough from point clouds and composes them for long-horizon tool-use manipulation.
how: Point-cloud scenes and tool-object interactions are modeled with GNNs; a tool classifier plus self-supervised policies plan multi-step manipulation.

lab_fit.note: Real-data learned simulators with action conditioning are directly re-runnable and scorable.

name: UniSim
title: Learning Interactive Real-World Simulators
output: action-conditioned video world model of real-world interaction
evaluation: Video prediction quality (FVD etc.) and usefulness for training VLA and RL policies purely in simulation, evaluated zero-shot on real robots.

generalization.note: Simulates outcomes of new high- and low-level actions; policies trained in it transfer to the real world.

summary: Generative video model trained on diverse real datasets to simulate visual outcomes of human and robot actions as a universal interactive simulator.
how: Heterogeneous data (robot, human video, navigation, internet) are unified into action-conditioned video diffusion that rolls out autoregressively.

lab_fit.note: Action-conditioned real simulator, but closed weights limit sandboxed re-runs.

name: Visual Particle Dynamics (VPD)
title: Learning 3D Particle-based Simulators from RGB-D Videos
output: latent-particle neural simulator with neural renderer
evaluation: Rendered rollout quality against held-out RGB-D trajectories, long-horizon prediction, novel-view rendering and scene editing versus 2D video prediction baselines.

generalization.note: Trained on two objects, it simulates 32-object scenes and edited scenes (objects removed) with novel views.

summary: End-to-end learns a 3D latent particle representation, a GNN simulator and a renderer directly from posed RGB-D videos without ground-truth state.
how: RGB-D frames are lifted to latent particles; a hierarchical GNN advances them in time and a neural renderer decodes images, trained with pixel losses only.

lab_fit.note: Observation-to-simulator pipeline with editable, re-renderable rollouts suits hidden-video scoring.

name: AdaptiGraph
title: AdaptiGraph: Material-Adaptive Graph-Based Neural Dynamics for Robotic Manipulation
output: property-conditioned GNN particle dynamics model with online physical-parameter adaptation
evaluation: Prediction error and real-robot manipulation success on boxes, ropes, granular media and cloth with unknown properties, after few-shot property inference.

generalization.note: Infers physical properties of unseen real objects from a few interactions and predicts their response to new actions.

summary: Graph-based neural dynamics conditioned on a physical-property variable, adapted online from few real interactions to model diverse deformable materials.
how: Trained across simulated materials with property conditioning; at test time properties are optimized from observed real interactions, then used for MPC.

lab_fit.note: Few-shot real interactions to an adapted simulator, scorable on held-out real rollouts.

name: GausSim
title: GausSim: Foreseeing Reality by Gaussian Simulator for Elastic Objects
output: neural simulator over Gaussian kernels for elastic objects
evaluation: Comparison of predicted future dynamics and renderings against ground-truth real multi-view videos (READY dataset) and physics-driven baselines.

generalization.note: Forecasts future deformation of real elastic objects beyond observed frames.

summary: Neural Gaussian-kernel simulator grounded in continuum mechanics that forecasts real elastic deformations, with the real-world READY multi-view dataset.
how: Gaussian kernels are grouped into hierarchical center-of-mass systems; a network predicts their coarse-to-fine motion with explicit mechanical constraints.

lab_fit.note: Real multi-view video to forward simulator compared with held-out future frames.

name: Genie 2
title: Genie 2: A large-scale foundation world model
output: action-controllable interactive 3D world rendered as video
evaluation: Qualitative demonstrations of consistency (up to ~1 minute), object interactions, water, smoke, gravity and lighting, and use for training embodied agents.

generalization.note: Generates interactive worlds from unseen prompt images, but physics accuracy is not quantitatively measured.

summary: Foundation world model generating keyboard/mouse-controllable 3D environments from a single image, with emergent physics such as gravity, water and lighting.
how: An autoregressive latent video model predicts the next observation given past frames and actions, trained on large-scale video.

lab_fit.note: Closed model with no public access for sandboxed evaluation.

name: GS-Dynamics
title: Dynamic 3D Gaussian Tracking for Graph-Based Neural Dynamics Modeling
output: action-conditioned GNN dynamics over 3D Gaussians with rendering
evaluation: 3D motion prediction and rendered action-conditioned video prediction on held-out real robot interactions with ropes, cloth and stuffed animals, plus model-based planning.

generalization.note: Predicts object responses to unseen robot actions and is used for action-conditioned video prediction and planning.

summary: Learns object dynamics directly from multi-view RGB videos of robot interactions via dynamic 3D Gaussian tracking and a particle GNN.
how: Dynamic 3D Gaussian Splatting tracks particles; a GNN on sparse control particles learns action-conditioned motion, interpolated to Gaussians for rendering.

lab_fit.note: Real multi-view video to re-runnable, renderable simulator; natural fit for hidden held-out rollouts.

name: IRASim
title: IRASim: A Fine-Grained World Model for Robot Manipulation
output: action-trajectory-conditioned video world model for manipulation
evaluation: Video quality metrics and trajectory alignment on real and simulated robot datasets, plus policy evaluation and planning within the world model.

generalization.note: Generates outcomes for new action trajectories, used to evaluate and improve policies.

summary: Diffusion-transformer world model generating fine-grained robot-object interaction videos aligned frame-by-frame with robot action trajectories.
how: A frame-level action-conditioning module in each transformer block ties every generated frame to the corresponding action.

lab_fit.note: Open action-conditioned simulator; outputs comparable to held-out real rollouts.

name: 1X World Model
title: 1X World Model
output: action-trajectory-conditioned video world model of a humanoid robot for policy evaluation
evaluation: Predicted task success of policy checkpoints correlated with real-world evaluation scores on home-environment tasks.

generalization.note: Simulates outcomes of new policies' actions from real initial frames and ranks them consistently with real-world results.

summary: Learned humanoid world model used as a simulator to evaluate robot policies offline, validated by correlation with real-world success rates.
how: Starting from real frames, the model generates futures steered by exact robot action trajectories; success predictions rank policy checkpoints. A public challenge releases tokenized real data and baselines.

lab_fit.note: Real-data simulator validated against real outcomes, but the production model is closed; only challenge baselines are open.

name: Cosmos
title: Cosmos World Foundation Model Platform for Physical AI
output: pretrained and post-trainable video world foundation models (diffusion and autoregressive)
evaluation: 3D consistency and physics-alignment tests against simulated ground truth, plus post-training for camera control, robot manipulation and driving.

generalization.note: Post-trained models predict outcomes for new actions/cameras, but physics alignment is reported as limited.

summary: Open-weight world foundation models trained on large-scale real video, post-trainable into action-conditioned simulators for robotics and driving.
how: Video tokenizers plus diffusion and autoregressive transformers are pretrained on curated physical-AI video and fine-tuned on domain data with action or camera conditioning.

lab_fit.note: Open weights allow sandboxed re-runs as an action-conditioned simulator baseline.

name: Ctrl-World
title: Ctrl-World: A Controllable Generative World Model for Robot Manipulation
output: multi-view action-conditioned video world model for policy rollouts
evaluation: Correlation between policy success rates imagined in the world model and real-world rollouts, plus real-robot gains after training on imagined successful trajectories.

generalization.note: Rolls out generalist policies on unfamiliar objects and instructions and predicts their real success.

summary: Controllable multi-view world model trained on real robot data that lets generalist policies roll out in imagination for evaluation and improvement.
how: Multi-view joint prediction with frame-level action conditioning and pose-conditioned memory retrieval keeps long closed-loop rollouts consistent.

lab_fit.note: Open action-conditioned real-data simulator validated against real policy outcomes.

name: DreamGen
title: DreamGen: Unlocking Generalization in Robot Learning through Video World Models
output: synthetic robot trajectories (videos plus inferred pseudo-actions) from a fine-tuned video world model
evaluation: Real-robot policy success on new behaviors and environments when trained on generated neural trajectories, plus the DreamGen Bench video-model benchmark.

generalization.note: Policies learn unseen verbs and environments from world-model generations starting from a single teleoperated task.

summary: Fine-tunes video world models on a robot's real data to synthesize trajectories for new behaviors and environments, enabling policy generalization.
how: A video model is adapted to the robot embodiment, prompted with images and instructions, and pseudo-actions are recovered by inverse dynamics or latent actions.

lab_fit.note: Generator is open, but its output is training data rather than a re-runnable simulator.

name: Genie 3
title: Genie 3: A new frontier for world models
output: real-time navigable interactive world video (720p, 24 fps)
evaluation: Qualitative demonstrations of minute-scale consistency, physical effects (water, lighting), promptable world events and agent training.

generalization.note: Supports promptable events and new actions, but physical fidelity is not quantitatively benchmarked.

summary: Real-time general-purpose world model generating navigable, consistent environments from text with promptable world events.
how: Autoregressive frame generation conditioned on prior frames and user actions, with emergent consistency rather than explicit 3D representations.

lab_fit.note: Limited research preview; cannot be re-run in a sandbox.

name: PGND
title: Particle-Grid Neural Dynamics for Learning Deformable Object Models from RGB-D Videos
output: hybrid particle-grid neural dynamics model with Gaussian Splatting rendering
evaluation: 3D prediction and rendering quality on sparse-view real RGB-D robot interactions versus learning-based and physics-based simulators, plus goal-conditioned planning.

generalization.note: Predicts dynamics under unseen actions and generalizes at category level to unseen object instances.

summary: Particle-grid hybrid neural dynamics learned from real RGB-D videos of ropes, cloth, stuffed animals and paper bags, forming a fully learned digital twin.
how: Particles carry object shape while a spatial grid enforces continuity in predicting velocities; Gaussian Splatting renders action-conditioned rollouts.

lab_fit.note: Real RGB-D in, re-runnable action-conditioned simulator out; strong fit for sandboxed scoring.

name: PIN-WM
title: PIN-WM: Learning Physics-INformed World Models for Non-Prehensile Manipulation
output: differentiable rigid-body world model with Gaussian Splatting rendering
evaluation: Physical-parameter identification and sim-to-real policy success on real push and flip tasks (75% / 65%) without real-world fine-tuning.

generalization.note: Policies trained in the identified world model transfer to the real robot under new task goals.

summary: Identifies a 3D rigid-body world model from few visual interactions via differentiable physics and rendering, then trains transferable non-prehensile policies.
how: Friction, restitution and other parameters are optimized through a differentiable simulator with a Gaussian Splatting rendering loss; perturbed digital cousins train robust RL policies.

lab_fit.note: Few real observations in, executable simulator out, verifiable by downstream policy and held-out rollouts.

name: V-JEPA 2
title: V-JEPA 2: Self-Supervised Video Models Enable Understanding, Prediction and Planning
output: latent action-conditioned world model (V-JEPA 2-AC) for planning
evaluation: Video understanding and anticipation benchmarks plus zero-shot real-robot pick-and-place via MPC in latent space after training on ~62 hours of unlabeled robot video.

generalization.note: Plans zero-shot on robots in new labs without task-specific data or rewards.

summary: Self-supervised joint-embedding video model whose action-conditioned variant serves as a latent world model for zero-shot robot planning.
how: Masked latent prediction pretraining on internet video; a post-trained action-conditioned predictor rolls out embeddings for goal-image MPC.

lab_fit.note: Predicts in latent space, so outputs are hard to score against raw hidden observations.

name: SimBench
title: SimBench: A Framework for Evaluating and Diagnosing LLM-Based Digital-Twin Generation for Multi-Physics Simulation
target_output: PyChrono simulation script (digital twin)
scale: 34 physical systems x 3 turns = 102 tasks; 33+ LLMs
evaluation: An LLM judge guided by rules and reference solutions scores generated Chrono scripts.

generalization.note: Scores the requested system only.

summary: Ranks LLMs on generating digital twins for the Chrono multi-physics simulator from natural-language requests.
how: Multi-turn tasks covering multibody, FEA, vehicles, robots and sensors; judged by an LLM with rules and human input.

lab_fit.note: Text input and LLM-judged; no observation-to-sim scoring.

name: 4DCodeBench
title: 4DCodeBench: Benchmarking Agents on Inverse Graphics of Dynamic Scenes
target_output: executable graphics program that reconstructs the dynamic 3D scene (4D world)
scale: 200 videos (100 real, 100 synthetic)
evaluation: Renders of the delivered world are compared with the reference on perceptual (DINOv3), 2D dynamics (flow, tracks, dynamic IoU), depth and, for synthetic cases, 3D geometry and trajectory metrics, plus mesh-quality checks and a VLM judge.

generalization.note: Scores reproduction of the observed clip only; no new initial states or interventions.

summary: Agents reconstruct dynamic scenes from video as executable graphics programs, covering deformation, fluid flow and fracture.
how: Curated real videos plus physics-simulated synthetic scenes; frontier models write code whose output is scored per appearance, geometry and dynamics family.

lab_fit.note: Already integrated in Real2SimLab.

name: DeformFieldBench
title: Physical-Field-Bridged Material Parameter Inference from Multi-View Deformation Videos
target_output: constitutive model type and material parameters
scale: 5,000 3DGS-MPM simulations, 100 shapes, 5 loading modes; 5 real sequences
evaluation: Median parameter error, constitutive-type classification, stress-hotspot recall and same-simulator replay SSIM/PSNR on unseen objects.

generalization.note: Replays and predicts future states on unseen objects.

summary: Synthetic multi-view benchmark for inferring simulation-ready material parameters of deformable objects.
how: 3DGS-MPM environment with elastic, von Mises and plasticine-like models; methods predict forces, flow and stress fields, then parameters.

lab_fit.note: Public data and programmatic scores, but output is parameters rather than a program.

name: IRIS
title: IRIS: A Real-World Benchmark for Inverse Recovery and Identification of Physical Dynamic Systems from Monocular Video
target_output: governing equation and physical parameters of the observed system
scale: 240 real 4K/60fps videos, 8 systems (dropping ball, pendulum, sliding cone, etc.)
evaluation: Parameter MAE against independently measured ground truth, equation-selection accuracy, identifiability, robustness and extrapolation error beyond the observed horizon.

generalization.note: Tests extrapolation beyond the observed time window.

summary: Real-world benchmark for recovering governing equations and physical parameters of single- and multi-body systems from monocular video.
how: Recorded real pendulums, falling/rolling objects and collisions with measured parameters and uncertainties; baselines include a multi-step physics loss and equation-identification strategies.

lab_fit.note: Already integrated in Real2SimLab.

name: MPMWorlds
title: MPMWorlds: Material-Point-Method Simulations for Inferring and Extrapolating Physical Dynamics
target_output: executable MPM simulation program (or future frames for video models)
scale: 2D MPM scenes: fluids, deformables, emitters, sand, snow
evaluation: Forward extrapolations are compared with ground-truth simulation via mask IoU and motion error over increasing horizons.

generalization.note: Scores extrapolation beyond the observed prefix.

summary: 2D MPM benchmark comparing VLM code generation with video diffusion for inferring and extrapolating continuum dynamics.
how: VLMs write MPM simulation code from short clips with varying side information; rollouts are compared with held-out future frames.

lab_fit.note: Good fit (code rollout vs hidden future) but dataset not yet public.

name: PhysCodeBench
title: PhysCodeBench: Benchmarking Physics-Aware Symbolic Simulation of 3D Scenes via Self-Corrective Multi-Agent Refinement
target_output: executable Genesis simulation code
scale: 1,200 expert-validated examples, 4 domains
evaluation: Physical correctness is checked from engine state via conservation-law residuals and expert-written assertions, with a MuJoCo cross-engine subset.

generalization.note: Checks the described scenario only.

summary: Text-to-simulation benchmark: turn natural-language descriptions of physical phenomena into executable 3D simulation code.
how: Expert reference implementations in Genesis; PhysCodeEval inspects simulator state rather than rendered pixels.

lab_fit.note: Input is text, not observations; data not yet released.

name: PhysCodeGym
title: PhysCodeGym: Benchmarking Coding Agents for Physically Verifiable 4D Reconstruction
target_output: Blender Python program that re-simulates the observed physical process
scale: 156 tasks (95 rigid, 40 liquid, 12 cloth, 9 wind); 43 with counterfactual checks
evaluation: Re-rendered output is scored on SSIM, LPIPS, object accuracy, events, motion and rubric-based physical validity (e.g. energy, support, penetration), combined into visual and physical scores.

generalization.note: 43 tasks apply counterfactual edits to the delivered scene and check that it stays physically consistent.

summary: Coding agents rebuild physical scenes from video as Blender programs, scored on visual and physical fidelity with counterfactual checks.
how: Reference clips from Physics-IQ, Pexels, IRIS and other sources are standardized; agents iterate with simulation feedback, then six metrics and rubric checks score the result.

lab_fit.note: Already integrated in Real2SimLab.

name: PhySimCode
title: PhySimCode: A Benchmark and Evaluation Method for Physics Video to Code Generation
target_output: runnable Python simulation (SciPy or PyBullet) that reproduces the video
scale: 160.6K generated samples, 162 phenomena; 2,430-video public eval set
evaluation: Scores physical-law correctness, parameter recovery within ±20%, compile/run/video-save rates, video similarity and human ratings of physics equivalence.

generalization.note: Compares against the observed video and its ground-truth parameters only.

summary: Given only a raw video, a model must identify the physics, recover parameter values and write runnable Python that reproduces it.
how: Procedurally generated SciPy 2D and PyBullet 3D scenes across 9 domains; ten MLLMs evaluated; best system recovers 7.7% of parameters within ±20%.

lab_fit.note: Already integrated in Real2SimLab.

name: SimuScene
title: Training and Benchmarking Code Generation for Physics-Inspired Animations
target_output: Python code that renders a physics animation video
scale: 7,659 scenarios, 52 concepts, 5 domains; 334-item human-verified test set
evaluation: Generated code is run to render a video and a VLM answers verification questions about whether the dynamics match the description (Avg@8, Pass@8).

generalization.note: Scores the described scenario only.

summary: Benchmark and RL training data for LLMs that write code simulating physical scenarios described in text (v1 title: SimuScene).
how: Text prompts across mechanics, optics, fluids and more; videos rendered from generated code are verified by a VLM, which also serves as an RL reward.

lab_fit.note: Text input; VLM-judged rather than reference-based scoring.

name: Video2World
title: Video2World: Benchmarking Coding Agents for Interactive World Modeling from Embodied Videos
target_output: simulated environment plus robot behaviour package that is replayed in simulation
scale: 222 instances from 189 robot and human videos, 39 task families
evaluation: Rebuilt environments are scored on geometric fidelity, dynamic fidelity (replay match) and functional task success.

generalization.note: Supports layout changes within a method-declared layout space, beyond pure replay.

summary: Coding agents watch an embodied video and build an interactive simulated world reproducing the scene and robot behaviour.
how: Treats video-to-simulation as software engineering with execution feedback; nine coding-agent systems compared against human-assisted reconstruction.

lab_fit.note: Already integrated in Real2SimLab.

name: VisPhyWorld / VisPhyBench
title: VisPhyWorld: Probing Physical Reasoning via Code-Driven Video Reconstruction
target_output: executable simulator code (e.g. Three.js / P5.js) that re-renders and continues the motion
scale: 209 scenes from 108 physical templates
evaluation: Re-simulated video is compared with ground truth using perceptual, semantic and optical-flow motion metrics, plus Gemini and human judges.

generalization.note: Code must forecast motion beyond the given key frames, but no interventions.

summary: MLLMs turn key frames into executable simulator code, making their inferred physics inspectable and testable via re-rendered video.
how: From two key frames plus optional detections, models write Three.js/P5.js code; outputs are rendered and compared with ground-truth motion.

lab_fit.note: Public data and programmatic metrics on a re-rendered executable output.

name: IntPhys
title: IntPhys: A Framework and Benchmark for Visual Intuitive Physics Reasoning
target_output: plausibility score for each video
scale: 15K training videos; test blocks of 3,600 movies
evaluation: Error in telling possible from impossible events within pixel-matched sets (object permanence, shape constancy, spatio-temporal continuity).

generalization.note: Violation-of-expectation detection only.

summary: Violation-of-expectation benchmark asking models to flag physically impossible events in game-engine videos.
how: Possible and impossible variants are pixel-matched so only temporal structure separates them; humans are tested on the same stimuli.

lab_fit.note: Plausibility scoring, no executable reconstruction.

name: PHYRE
title: PHYRE: A New Benchmark for Physical Reasoning
target_output: action that solves a 2D physics puzzle
scale: 2 tiers of 2D classical-mechanics puzzle templates
evaluation: AUCCESS: success as a function of the number of simulator attempts, on within- and cross-template splits.

generalization.note: Cross-template splits test unseen puzzle types.

summary: Interactive 2D physics puzzles where an agent places objects so that a goal condition is met when the simulation runs.
how: Tasks come from templates with varied initial scenes; agents may try several actions in the simulator and are scored on attempts needed.

lab_fit.note: Simulator-in-the-loop but synthetic; not an observation-to-sim task.

name: CLEVRER
title: CLEVRER: CoLlision Events for Video REpresentation and Reasoning
target_output: answers to descriptive, explanatory, predictive and counterfactual questions
scale: 20,000 videos, 300K+ questions
evaluation: Per-question accuracy (per-option for multiple choice) by question type.

generalization.note: Counterfactual questions ask what happens if an object is removed.

summary: Video QA benchmark of colliding objects testing descriptive, explanatory, predictive and counterfactual reasoning.
how: Synthetic CLEVR-style collision videos with programmatically generated questions and simulator ground truth.

lab_fit.note: Counterfactuals could be answered by re-running a reconstructed sim; output is QA.

name: CoPhy
title: CoPhy: Counterfactual Learning of Physical Dynamics
target_output: object trajectories after a modified initial state
scale: 3 scenarios: BlocktowerCF, BallsCF, CollisionCF
evaluation: Error of predicted object positions in the counterfactual rollout against simulator ground truth.

generalization.note: Every example asks for the outcome under a changed initial state.

summary: Counterfactual dynamics benchmark: observe a sequence, then predict the outcome after the initial state is modified.
how: Each example pairs an observed sequence (AB) with an intervened start (C) and its outcome (D); confounders such as mass and friction are hidden.

lab_fit.note: Explicit interventions with trajectory ground truth; a delivered sim can be re-run from C and scored.

name: Physion
title: Physion: Evaluating Physical Prediction from Vision in Humans and Machines
target_output: prediction of whether two objects will come into contact
scale: 8 scenarios, 1,200 test movies (150 per scenario)
evaluation: Object Contact Prediction accuracy via a linear readout, compared with human accuracy and responses.

generalization.note: Predicts the unseen continuation; no interventions.

summary: Measures whether vision models predict physical outcomes like humans across eight scenarios (support, roll, link, drop, dominoes, contain, collide, drape).
how: TDW-rendered movies are cut before the outcome; models and humans predict whether a red agent object touches a yellow patient.

lab_fit.note: Outcome labels are programmatic; an agent's sim could answer by rollout, but no executable output is scored.

name: ComPhy
title: ComPhy: Compositional Physical Reasoning of Objects and Events from Videos
target_output: answers to factual, counterfactual and predictive questions
scale: 12K video sets (~60K videos), 99,844 questions
evaluation: Question-answering accuracy by question type.

generalization.note: Counterfactual and predictive questions require using inferred mass and charge.

summary: Tests inferring hidden properties (mass, charge) from a few reference videos and using them for compositional physical reasoning.
how: Each target video comes with four reference videos revealing object properties; questions are generated with simulator ground truth.

lab_fit.note: Hidden-parameter inference suits real2sim; output is QA.

name: CRAFT
title: CRAFT: A Benchmark for Causal Reasoning About Forces and inTeractions
target_output: answers to causal and counterfactual questions
scale: 9,917 videos, 57,524 questions, 20 environments
evaluation: Question-answering accuracy over descriptive, counterfactual and causal (cause/enable/prevent) questions.

generalization.note: Counterfactual questions ask about outcomes under removed objects.

summary: 2D physics video QA benchmark on causal reasoning about forces and object interactions.
how: Videos from a 2D simulator with programmatically generated questions grounded in simulation traces.

lab_fit.note: Counterfactuals answerable by rollout; QA output.

name: Physion++
title: Physion++: Evaluating Physical Scene Understanding that Requires Online Inference of Different Physical Properties
target_output: collision prediction after inferring hidden physical properties
scale: 9 scenarios over mass, friction, elasticity, deformability
evaluation: Contact-prediction accuracy and correlation with human responses, split into easy and hard trials.

generalization.note: Properties inferred online must be used to predict an unseen outcome.

summary: Extends Physion to outcomes that depend on latent properties (mass, friction, elasticity, deformability) that must be inferred from dynamics.
how: Each video has an inference period revealing properties and a prediction period; models predict contact and are compared with humans.

lab_fit.note: Good real2sim probe (hidden parameters); QA-style output.

name: ContPhy
title: ContPhy: Continuum Physical Concept Learning and Reasoning from Videos
target_output: answers to property and dynamics questions
scale: 4 scenarios: fluid hourglass, rope-pulley, cloth, soft balls
evaluation: Question-answering accuracy on physical-property and dynamics questions.

generalization.note: Some questions require predicting outcomes beyond the clip.

summary: Video reasoning benchmark on continuum materials (fluids, ropes, cloth, soft bodies) rather than rigid objects.
how: Simulated scenes with varied physical parameters and generated questions; also proposes the ContPRO oracle model.

lab_fit.note: Covers soft/fluid physics; QA output only.

name: IntPhys 2
title: IntPhys 2: Benchmarking Intuitive Physics Understanding In Complex Synthetic Environments
target_output: plausibility judgement for each video
scale: 1,416 videos (Main 1,012; Held-Out 344; Debug 60)
evaluation: Accuracy at telling possible from impossible videos across permanence, immutability, spatio-temporal continuity and solidity; held-out split via leaderboard.

generalization.note: Violation-of-expectation detection only.

summary: Harder successor to IntPhys with complex synthetic scenes; most models perform near chance while humans are near perfect.
how: Unreal-rendered scenes with static and moving cameras grouped into Easy/Medium/Hard; metadata withheld for the held-out split.

lab_fit.note: Plausibility scoring, no executable reconstruction.

name: PhysBench
title: PhysBench: Benchmarking and Enhancing Vision-Language Models for Physical World Understanding
target_output: answer to multiple-choice question
scale: 10,002 items, 4 domains, 19 subclasses
evaluation: Multiple-choice accuracy across 19 sub-tasks; 75 VLMs evaluated.

generalization.note: Static QA without interventions on a built model.

summary: Large VLM benchmark on physical object properties, relationships, scene understanding and dynamics.
how: Interleaved video-image-text questions grouped into four domains and eight capability dimensions; also proposes the PhysAgent framework.

lab_fit.note: QA output only.

name: CausalPhys
title: Causal Scaffolding for Physical Reasoning: A Benchmark for Causally-Informed Physical World Understanding in VLMs
target_output: answers with chain-of-thought rationales
scale: 3,062 questions from 11 public datasets
evaluation: Question-answering accuracy plus a causal-graph-grounded score for chain-of-thought alignment.

generalization.note: Includes intervention and anticipation questions.

summary: VLM benchmark on perception, anticipation, intervention and goal-oriented physical reasoning with expert causal graphs.
how: Clips from datasets such as EPIC-Kitchens and Ego4D are annotated with questions and causal graphs used to grade reasoning.

lab_fit.note: QA on real clips; no executable output.

name: PhysVista
title: PhysVista: Benchmarking Physical Intelligence in VLMs via a Perception-Reasoning-Assessment Loop
target_output: answers, violation time spans and plausibility ratings
scale: 2,060 questions across 13 tasks
evaluation: Multiple-choice accuracy, Micro-F1, temporal IoU for violation localization, and SRCC/PLCC for plausibility scores.

generalization.note: Includes counterfactual and prediction questions.

summary: Tests VLMs on perceiving physical state, reasoning about dynamics and judging plausibility of real and AI-generated videos.
how: Tasks span perception, dynamics reasoning (order, mechanism, violation, prediction, counterfactual) and plausibility assessment.

lab_fit.note: QA output only.

name: PhyGenBench
title: Towards World Simulator: Crafting Physical Commonsense-Based Benchmark for Video Generation
output: text-to-video generation of physical phenomena
scale: 160 prompts over 27 physical laws in 4 domains
evaluation: PhyGenEval, a hierarchical VLM/LLM-based evaluator checking key physical phenomena, ordering and overall naturalness, validated against human ratings.

generalization.note: Checks whether generated clips depict expected phenomena; no held-out real outcome.

summary: Physical-commonsense prompt benchmark for T2V models covering mechanics, optics, thermal and material properties with an automated hierarchical evaluator.
how: Each prompt implies a physical law; PhyGenEval asks VLMs staged questions about key frames and transitions to score adherence.

lab_fit.note: Text-conditioned and judge-scored; little to re-simulate.

name: PhyWorld
title: How Far is Video Generation from World Model: A Physical Law Perspective
output: future frames of 2D simulated object motion from initial frames
scale: 2D simulator with 30K-3M training videos; PHYRE-based 70-template combinatorial set
evaluation: Velocity error between simulator ground truth and motion parsed from generated videos for in-/out-of-distribution, plus FVD/SSIM/PSNR/LPIPS and human abnormal ratio for combinatorial generalization.

generalization.note: Explicitly tests out-of-distribution extrapolation (unseen velocities/sizes) and held-out combinatorial templates.

summary: Controlled study showing video diffusion models trained on simulated physics generalize in-distribution but fail to extrapolate physical laws out of distribution.
how: Diffusion video models are trained on deterministic 2D simulations (uniform motion, elastic collision, parabola) and tested on in-distribution, OOD and combinatorial splits with quantitative velocity checks.

lab_fit.note: Quantitative, simulator-verified references fit hidden-reference scoring, but data are synthetic 2D rather than real observations.

name: VideoPhy
title: VideoPhy: Evaluating Physical Commonsense for Video Generation
output: text-to-video generation of material interactions
scale: 688 captions of solid-solid, solid-fluid, fluid-fluid interactions
evaluation: Human annotators and the VideoCon-Physics auto-rater score semantic adherence and physical commonsense of generated videos.

generalization.note: Judges plausibility of generated clips; no ground-truth outcome or intervention is compared.

summary: Prompt benchmark judging whether text-to-video models respect physical commonsense in everyday material interactions.
how: Curated captions describing interactions are rendered by T2V models; humans and a trained video-language judge rate semantic adherence and physical commonsense.

lab_fit.note: Text-only input with judge-based scoring; no real observation or hidden physical reference.

name: WorldSimBench
title: WorldSimBench: Towards Video Generation Models as World Simulators
output: embodied video predictions convertible to control signals
scale: 3 embodied scenarios (open-ended environment, driving, robot manipulation) with HF-Embodied human feedback dataset
evaluation: Explicit perceptual evaluation with a human-preference-trained evaluator plus implicit manipulative evaluation by converting generated video into actions and measuring closed-loop task success.

generalization.note: Closed-loop control tests usefulness in new episodes, though not physical counterfactuals directly.

summary: Dual evaluation of video generators as embodied world simulators via human-aligned perceptual scoring and video-to-action closed-loop task success.
how: Generated videos are judged by a learned evaluator and also turned into control signals via inverse dynamics to execute tasks in simulators.

lab_fit.note: Downstream-control scoring is sandbox-compatible, but conditioning is not real-to-sim reconstruction.

name: Morpheus
title: Evaluating Newtonian Mechanics in Video Generative Models with Real Physical Systems
output: video continuation of real lab experiments
scale: 130 real videos of Newtonian systems (pendulums, collisions, projectiles, springs, rolling/sliding objects)
evaluation: Physics-informed scores (dynamical and physical-invariance) from tracked trajectories checking conservation laws and equations of motion, plus discard rates for vanishing/duplicating objects.

generalization.note: Generations conditioned on real experiments are checked against governing laws rather than a single trajectory, so any plausible continuation is admissible.

summary: Real-experiment benchmark scoring video generators with physics-informed invariants instead of human or VLM judgments.
how: Real recordings of conservation-governed systems condition generation; tracked object trajectories are fit to equations of motion to test invariance.

lab_fit.note: Real observations, quantitative physics-informed scoring and hidden continuations map directly onto sandboxed re-run and scoring.

name: PhyCoBench
title: A Physical Coherence Benchmark for Evaluating Video Generation Models via Optical Flow-guided Frame Prediction
output: text-to-video generation
scale: 120 prompts over 7 categories of physical principles
evaluation: PhyCoPredictor, an optical-flow-guided frame-prediction diffusion model, scores physical coherence; ranking agreement with manual evaluation is reported.

generalization.note: Measures coherence of generated clips; no held-out real outcome.

summary: Physical-coherence T2V benchmark with an automatic evaluator that predicts optical flow and frames to detect implausible motion.
how: A learned predictor forecasts flow and frames from generated videos; deviation between prediction and generation indicates incoherent physics.

lab_fit.note: Text prompts and learned evaluator; no real reference.

name: Physics-IQ
title: Do generative video models understand physical principles?
output: continuation video of a real filmed physical event (i2v or multi-frame v2v)
scale: real videos, every scenario from 3 views x 2 takes, 4K / 30 fps
evaluation: Generated continuations are compared to held-out real footage with motion-mask metrics (spatial IoU, spatiotemporal IoU, weighted spatial IoU, MSE) combined into a Physics-IQ score normalized by physical variance between real takes.

generalization.note: Models must predict unseen real outcomes of novel scenarios from a conditioning prefix; the true future is hidden.

summary: Real-world filmed benchmark testing whether video models can predict what physically happens next across solid mechanics, fluids, optics, magnetism and thermodynamics.
how: A video model is given the first seconds of a real recorded experiment and must generate the continuation; motion masks of generated and real futures are compared against the variability between two real takes.

lab_fit.note: Already integrated in Real2SimLab.

name: PhyWorldBench
title: "PhyWorldBench": A Comprehensive Evaluation of Physical Realism in Text-to-Video Models
output: text-to-video generation of physical phenomena, including anti-physics prompts
scale: 1,050 prompts in 10 categories x 5 subcategories; 12,600 videos from 12 models
evaluation: Large-scale human evaluation plus a Context-Aware Prompt (CAP) MLLM zero-shot judge of physical realism.

generalization.note: Anti-Physics prompts test following counterfactual rules, but no real ground-truth outcome.

summary: Large T2V physics benchmark spanning fundamental to composite phenomena plus an Anti-Physics category of deliberately law-violating prompts.
how: Each scenario has event, physics-enhanced and narrative prompts; humans and an MLLM with context-aware prompting judge physical realism.

lab_fit.note: Text-only, judge-scored.

name: T2VPhysBench
title: T2VPhysBench: A First-Principles Benchmark for Physical Consistency in Text-to-Video Generation
output: text-to-video generation obeying a specified physical law
scale: 12 physical laws (Newtonian mechanics, conservation, phenomenological); 10 T2V models
evaluation: Three human annotators grade each generated video; per-law scores averaged over prompts, plus prompt-hinting and counterfactual-prompt ablations.

generalization.note: Includes counterfactual prompts asking models to violate laws, but no real reference outcome.

summary: First-principles T2V benchmark finding all tested models score below 0.6 on twelve core physical laws, with physics hints giving negligible gains.
how: Prompts target specific laws (collisions, energy conservation, gravity); human raters score physical consistency per law.

lab_fit.note: Human-rated text prompts; no observations or hidden references.

name: VideoPhy-2
title: VideoPhy-2: A Challenging Action-Centric Physical Commonsense Evaluation in Video Generation
output: text-to-video generation of real-world actions
scale: 200 actions with detailed prompts; human-annotated train/test sets
evaluation: Human evaluation of semantic adherence, physical commonsense and per-rule grounding, plus a released automatic rater.

generalization.note: Plausibility judgment of generated clips; no hidden real outcome.

summary: Action-centric successor to VideoPhy with fine-grained physical-rule annotations, finding conservation laws are frequently violated by modern generators.
how: Prompts depicting 200 actions (e.g., sports, tool use) are generated by T2V models and rated by humans and an AutoRater for physics rule violations.

lab_fit.note: Judge-based on text prompts; no real observations to reconstruct.

name: WorldModelBench
title: WorldModelBench: Judging Video Generation Models As World Models
output: image+text-conditioned video continuation in application domains
scale: 350 image-text conditions across 7 domains / 56 subdomains; 67K human labels
evaluation: Human labels and a fine-tuned 2B VLM judge score instruction following, common sense and physics adherence (e.g., mass conservation, penetration).

generalization.note: Models must extrapolate from a real first frame, but scoring is violation detection rather than comparison to a true outcome.

summary: Benchmark judging video generators as world models in robotics, driving, industry, gaming and nature, focusing on subtle physics violations.
how: Generators continue first frames under text instructions; a human-aligned VLM judger flags instruction failures and physical-law violations.

lab_fit.note: Real conditioning frames, but no hidden ground-truth future; scoring relies on a judge model.

name: WorldScore
title: WorldScore: A Unified Evaluation Benchmark for World Generation
output: next-scene world generation (3D/4D scene or video) following a camera trajectory
scale: 3,000 test examples, static and dynamic, indoor/outdoor, photoreal and stylized; 19 models
evaluation: Automatic metrics for controllability (camera/object), quality (consistency, photometric, style) and dynamics (motion accuracy, magnitude, smoothness).

generalization.note: Generators must produce unseen viewpoints and motion, but physics is only a small part of the dynamics score.

summary: Unified benchmark evaluating 3D, 4D and video world generators on controllability, quality and dynamics via camera-specified next-scene tasks.
how: World generation is decomposed into next-scene tasks with explicit camera layouts; automatic metrics measure control, quality and motion.

lab_fit.note: Image-conditioned with automatic metrics; physics coverage is shallow.

name: Apple-π
title: Apple-π: Benchmarking Thinking with Video Towards Law-Grounded Physical Intelligence
output: chain-of-frames video reasoning trace solving a classical-mechanics task
scale: Orchard: 400 videos over 10 classical-mechanics tasks (single-law and multi-law); 11 models
evaluation: Three-stage protocol (perception, formulation, deduction) scored by MLLM judges plus physics-law-grounded objective measures.

generalization.note: Multi-law tasks probe generalization beyond single-law cases.

summary: Benchmark treating generated video as a reasoning trace and checking whether video models solve mechanics tasks through law-grounded steps.
how: Infographic-annotated first frames prompt chain-of-frames generation; stage-resolved MLLM and objective physics measures diagnose where reasoning fails.

lab_fit.note: Reasoning-trace evaluation rather than simulation of real observations.

name: CRONOS
title: CRONOS: Benchmarking Counterfactual Physical Consistency in Video Models
output: video prediction of a physical event under controlled interventions
scale: Unreal Engine videos of falls, collisions and occlusions with interventions on viewpoint, scene, object category and appearance
evaluation: Prediction quality for the same physical event is compared across single-factor interventions (camera, scene, category, appearance) in I2V and V2V settings, with multiple plausible outcomes sampled.

generalization.note: Directly tests whether predictions stay physically consistent under controlled counterfactual changes.

summary: Intervention-based benchmark testing whether video world models' physical predictions are invariant to viewpoint, scene and appearance changes.
how: Photorealistic Unreal scenes hold the physical event fixed while varying one visual factor at a time; prediction quality across variants reveals reliance on superficial cues.

lab_fit.note: Counterfactual hidden references are a good match, but scenes are synthetic.

name: PhyGround
title: PhyGround: Benchmarking Physical Reasoning in Generative World Models
output: text+image-to-video generation with an expected physical outcome
scale: 250 prompts with expected outcomes over 13 physical laws; 8 models; 459 annotators, 37.4K fine-grained labels
evaluation: Quality-controlled human study with per-law observable sub-questions on a 1-5 scale, plus the released PhyJudge-9B automatic judge.

generalization.note: Prompts carry an expected outcome, but verification is by human/VLM judgment rather than measured reference.

summary: Criteria-grounded benchmark with per-law sub-questions and a large controlled human study, plus an open physics-aware video judge.
how: Each prompt is tied to an expected outcome and laws across solid mechanics, fluids and optics; annotators and PhyJudge-9B answer law-specific observable questions.

lab_fit.note: Judge-based scoring of generated clips; no real observation to rebuild.

name: Principia
title: Principia: Relational Physics Tests for Video Models
output: video of paired objects obeying the same Newtonian law

evaluation: Calibration-independent relational consistency score between paired objects computed in image space; VLMs are also tested on detecting relational violations.

generalization.note: Relational checks score any generated outcome against physical law without a single ground-truth trajectory.

summary: Real-scene benchmark testing Newtonian physics in video models through calibration-free relational consistency between paired objects; no model exceeds 0.42.
how: Two objects under the same law must move in predictable relation (e.g., equal fall acceleration); tracked image-space motions yield a violation score independent of frame rate and scale.

lab_fit.note: Real recordings and quantitative calibration-free physics scoring fit a sandboxed scorer well.
