scale: 2,000+ trajectories, 100+ objects, 86 synchronized views
evaluation: Used to test dynamic NeRF reconstruction and multi-view policy learning on real robot interactions with diverse materials.

generalization.note: Dataset; no evaluation protocol of its own for real-to-sim generalization.

summary: Dense multi-view recordings of a robot manipulating 100+ objects of 20+ materials, including liquids with different viscosity and density.
how: 86 DSLR cameras on a half-dome plus RealSense depth cameras and audio record robot interactions, with joint states and torques logged at 30 Hz.

name: RBO Dataset
title: The RBO Dataset of Articulated Objects and Interactions
scale: 14 objects, 358 RGB-D sequences (67 min), 78 with wrenches
evaluation: Used to evaluate articulation estimation and kinematic model identification from real interaction videos.

generalization.note: Dataset; no evaluation protocol of its own for real-to-sim generalization.

summary: Models of 14 everyday articulated objects plus RGB-D videos of people manipulating them, with motion-capture part poses and interaction wrenches.
how: Humans interact with the objects under varied lighting, viewpoints and backgrounds; motion capture gives ground-truth part poses and a force-torque sensor records wrenches.

name: YCB Object and Model Set
title: Benchmarking in Manipulation Research: The YCB Object and Model Set and Benchmarking Protocols
scale: everyday objects across several categories, each with RGB-D scans, meshes and physical properties
evaluation: Standard physical object set whose scanned models are imported into simulators as digital twins of real tabletop objects.

generalization.note: Dataset; no evaluation protocol of its own for real-to-sim generalization.

summary: Physical everyday objects distributed to labs with matching high-resolution RGB-D scans, mesh models and physical properties such as mass.
how: Each object is turntable-scanned with RGB-D and high-resolution cameras to produce textured meshes; physical properties are recorded alongside.

name: Google Scanned Objects
title: Google Scanned Objects: A High-Quality Dataset of 3D Scanned Household Items
scale: 1,030 scanned household objects
evaluation: Widely used as simulation-ready rigid assets for robot learning and as real-object priors in reconstruction.

generalization.note: Dataset; no evaluation protocol of its own for real-to-sim generalization.

summary: Over a thousand high-quality 3D scans of real household items, preprocessed for direct use in Gazebo and Bullet.
how: Objects were scanned with a structured-light pipeline into watertight textured meshes and packaged with simulator metadata.

name: ABO
title: ABO: Dataset and Benchmarks for Real-World 3D Object Understanding
scale: 147,702 products; 7,900+ 3D models with PBR materials
evaluation: Source of material-annotated 3D objects; its ABO-500 subset is used for physical property (mass) estimation in real2sim work.

generalization.note: Dataset; no evaluation protocol of its own for real-to-sim generalization.

summary: Amazon product catalog with images, metadata including item weight, and artist-made 3D models with physically based materials.
how: Product listings from Amazon provide multi-view images and metadata; artists created matching 3D models with PBR material maps.

name: MultiScan
title: MultiScan: Scalable RGBD scanning for 3D environments with articulated objects
scale: 273 scans, 117 scenes, 10,957 objects, 5,129 parts
evaluation: Used to train and test part segmentation and mobility (articulation) estimation on real indoor scans.

generalization.note: Dataset; no evaluation protocol of its own for real-to-sim generalization.

summary: Real RGB-D scans of indoor scenes with textured meshes, part and object labels, and part mobility parameters for articulated objects.
how: Scenes are scanned with phones and tablets, reconstructed into meshes, and annotated with semantic parts and articulation axes and types.

name: OPDReal
title: OPD: Single-view 3D Openable Part Detection
scale: OPDReal (real RGB-D reconstructions) + OPDSynth
evaluation: Used to evaluate detection of openable parts and their motion parameters from a single real image.

generalization.note: Dataset; no evaluation protocol of its own for real-to-sim generalization.

summary: Real-object RGB-D reconstructions annotated with openable parts and motion parameters, released with a synthetic counterpart (OPDSynth).
how: Real objects are reconstructed from RGB-D scans and annotated with part masks, motion type, axis and origin.

name: AKB-48
title: AKB-48: A Real-World Articulated Object Knowledge Base
scale: 2,037 articulated object models, 48 categories
evaluation: Used for articulated pose estimation, reconstruction and manipulation with physics-annotated real-object models.

generalization.note: Dataset; no evaluation protocol of its own for real-to-sim generalization.

summary: Knowledge base of 2,037 scanned real articulated objects whose knowledge graphs record geometry, kinematics and physical properties.
how: Real objects are scanned and modeled with the FArM pipeline in 10-15 minutes each, filling an articulation knowledge graph (ArtiKG).

name: ArtVIP
title: ArtVIP: Articulated Digital Assets of Visual Realism, Modular Interaction, and Physical Fidelity for Robot Learning
institution: Beijing Innovation Center of Humanoid Robotics
scale: 900+ digital-twin articulated objects, 6 digital-twin scenes
evaluation: Used as sim-ready articulated assets for imitation and reinforcement learning with sim-to-real transfer.

generalization.note: Dataset; no evaluation protocol of its own for real-to-sim generalization.

summary: Professionally modeled digital twins of real articulated objects in USD, with tuned joint dynamics and embedded interaction semantics.
how: Modelers build assets under a unified spec; physical fidelity of joints is checked against real objects with optical motion capture.

name: BEHAVIOR-1K Assets
title: BEHAVIOR-1K: A Human-Centered, Embodied AI Benchmark with 1,000 Everyday Activities and Realistic Simulation
scale: 9,000+ objects across 50 scenes
evaluation: Asset library used as simulation-ready objects and scenes, with physical and semantic annotations, in OmniGibson.

generalization.note: Dataset; no evaluation protocol of its own for real-to-sim generalization.

summary: Large library of simulation-ready objects and scenes annotated with physical and semantic properties, built for the OmniGibson simulator.
how: Objects and 50 scenes are modeled and annotated with physical and semantic properties to support rigid, deformable and liquid simulation.

name: Articulate3D
title: Articulate3D: Holistic Understanding of 3D Scenes as Universal Scene Description
scale: 280 real indoor scenes, 8 annotation types
evaluation: Used to train and test articulation and part understanding in real scans exported as simulation-ready USD scenes.

generalization.note: Dataset; no evaluation protocol of its own for real-to-sim generalization.

summary: Real indoor scans annotated with parts, articulation parameters, connectivity and object mass, released as simulation-ready USD scenes.
how: Experts annotate ScanNet++ scenes with part segmentation, motion type, axis, origin and range, part connectivity and mass.

name: Aria Digital Twin
title: Aria Digital Twin: A New Benchmark Dataset for Egocentric 3D Machine Perception
scale: 200+ sequences in 2 real indoor spaces, ~400 digital-twin objects
evaluation: Used for sim-to-real and reconstruction studies where real egocentric recordings align with a full digital twin of the scene.

generalization.note: Dataset; no evaluation protocol of its own for real-to-sim generalization.

summary: Real egocentric recordings in two indoor spaces paired with a complete digital twin providing object poses, depth, segmentation and synthetic renders.
how: Aria glasses record real activities; scenes and objects are digitized so every frame has ground-truth 6DoF poses and matching simulated renders.

name: Digital Twin Catalog
title: Digital Twin Catalog: A Large-Scale Photorealistic 3D Object Digital Twin Dataset
scale: 2,000+ scanned objects; DSLR and Aria captures
evaluation: Used to evaluate object digital-twin reconstruction (geometry, PBR materials, relighting) against real captures.

generalization.note: Dataset; no evaluation protocol of its own for real-to-sim generalization.

summary: Millimeter-accurate digital twins of real objects with PBR materials, paired with real DSLR and egocentric Aria image sequences.
how: Objects are scanned to twin quality; real captures under varied lighting with masks and environment maps support comparison with renders.

name: ReplicaCAD
title: Habitat 2.0: Training Home Assistants to Rearrange their Habitat
scale: 6 rooms, 92 objects, recreated real apartment
evaluation: Used as an interactive digital twin of a real scanned apartment for rearrangement and sim-to-real studies.

generalization.note: Dataset; no evaluation protocol of its own for real-to-sim generalization.

summary: Artist-built interactive replica of the real Replica FRL apartment, with collision shapes, physical parameters and articulated furniture.
how: Artists rebuilt the scanned apartment as separate objects with semantic labels, physics parameters and articulation (900+ person-hours).

name: LiDARsim
title: LiDARsim: Realistic LiDAR Simulation by Leveraging the Real World
output: LiDAR simulator built from a catalog of reconstructed real 3D maps and dynamic objects
evaluation: Compares simulated vs. real LiDAR for realism and perception-model domain gap, and uses the simulator for long-tail perception testing and closed-loop evaluation.

generalization.note: Scenarios place the ego vehicle and catalog actors in new configurations not present in any log, including closed-loop runs.

summary: Builds realistic LiDAR simulation from fleet-collected real scans instead of CAD worlds, combining ray casting with a learned correction network.
how: Surfel maps and object meshes are reconstructed from real LiDAR sweeps; ray casting over composed scenes is refined by a network that predicts ray drop and deviations.

name: UniSim (Waabi)
title: UniSim: A Neural Closed-Loop Sensor Simulator
output: neural closed-loop sensor simulator (cameras + LiDAR) with removable, insertable and re-routed actors
evaluation: Measures camera and LiDAR novel-view realism on PandaSet (PSNR, FID, detection agreement) and runs closed-loop safety-critical scenarios with an autonomy system.

generalization.note: Renders lane changes, actor insertion/removal and modified actor routes, and drives an autonomy stack in closed loop.

summary: Converts a single recorded driving log into a manipulable multi-sensor digital twin for closed-loop testing of self-driving vehicles.
how: Neural feature grids reconstruct static background and each dynamic actor separately; composited features are volume-rendered and decoded by a CNN, with a learned prior to complete unseen regions.

name: MARS
title: MARS: An Instance-aware, Modular and Realistic Simulator for Autonomous Driving
output: open-source NeRF driving simulator with separately controllable foreground instances
evaluation: Reports novel-view synthesis quality (PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS) on KITTI and Virtual KITTI 2 and shows qualitative instance editing.

generalization.note: Instance trajectories and appearance can be edited, but quantitative tests stay on held-out frames of the log.

summary: Modular, instance-aware NeRF simulator for autonomous driving that lets users control each vehicle's appearance and trajectory.
how: Background and each tracked instance get independent NeRFs with swappable backbones and samplers; samples are composed and rendered to RGB, depth and semantics.

name: NeuRAD
title: NeuRAD: Neural Rendering for Autonomous Driving
output: neural camera + LiDAR renderer for driving logs with editable ego pose and actors
evaluation: Evaluates camera and LiDAR rendering on five driving datasets (nuScenes, PandaSet, Argoverse 2, KITTI, ZOD), including FID under shifted ego and actor poses.

generalization.note: Tests rendering under ego lane shifts and actor edits, but no closed-loop driving in the paper itself.

summary: Single neural field tailored to driving data, modelling rolling shutter, beam divergence and ray drop for sensor-realistic camera and LiDAR rendering.
how: A hash-grid neural feature field with per-actor boxes is optimized jointly on camera and LiDAR; sensor-specific effects are modelled explicitly and a CNN decodes features to images.

name: EmerNeRF
title: EmerNeRF: Emergent Spatial-Temporal Scene Decomposition via Self-Supervision
output: self-supervised static/dynamic/flow neural field of a driving scene for sensor simulation
evaluation: Measures scene reconstruction and novel-view synthesis on a 120-sequence Waymo benchmark (NOTR), plus occupancy prediction from lifted foundation-model features.

generalization.note: Renders held-out timesteps and views of the same log; no actor editing or closed-loop use.

summary: Decomposes driving scenes into static and dynamic fields with an emergent flow field, learned purely by self-supervision without box annotations.
how: Static, dynamic and induced flow fields are jointly optimized from camera and LiDAR; flow aggregates multi-frame features to sharpen dynamic objects.

name: Street Gaussians
title: Street Gaussians: Modeling Dynamic Urban Scenes with Gaussian Splatting
output: composable 3DGS street scene with per-vehicle Gaussian models supporting edits, rendered in real time
evaluation: Compares novel-view rendering quality and speed on Waymo and KITTI and demonstrates vehicle editing (swap, translate, remove).

generalization.note: Supports scene edits such as moving or replacing vehicles, but quantitative tests are held-out frames of the log.

summary: Explicit 3D Gaussian representation of dynamic urban streets with separately optimized vehicle models, trained in half an hour and rendered at 135 FPS.
how: Background and each tracked vehicle are 3D Gaussian point clouds initialized from LiDAR; vehicle poses are refined during optimization and dynamic appearance uses 4D spherical harmonics.

name: DrivingGaussian
title: DrivingGaussian: Composite Gaussian Splatting for Surrounding Dynamic Autonomous Driving Scenes
output: surround-view 3DGS reconstruction of dynamic driving scenes with per-object Gaussian graph
evaluation: Evaluates surround-view novel-view synthesis on nuScenes and KITTI-360 against NeRF and 3DGS baselines.

generalization.note: Shows inserting and composing objects in reconstructed scenes, but metrics are on views from the log.

summary: Composite Gaussian Splatting for 360-degree surround-view driving scenes, combining incremental static background with a dynamic Gaussian graph for moving objects.
how: Static background is built incrementally from sequential frames with a LiDAR prior; each moving object is reconstructed separately and placed via a composite dynamic Gaussian graph.

name: OmniRe
title: OmniRe: Omni Urban Scene Reconstruction
output: 3DGS digital twin of urban scenes with vehicles, pedestrians and cyclists as controllable actors
evaluation: Measures reconstruction and novel-view synthesis on Waymo and five more driving datasets, and demonstrates human-behaviour and human-vehicle interaction simulation.

generalization.note: Actors including pedestrians can be re-animated for new interactions, but evaluation is mostly reconstruction quality on the log.

summary: Holistic driving-scene digital twin that reconstructs every dynamic actor class, including non-rigid pedestrians, from on-device logs.
how: A 3DGS scene graph holds background, rigid vehicles and SMPL-driven or deformable Gaussians for humans in canonical spaces, all optimized from camera and LiDAR.

name: HUGSIM
title: HUGSIM: A Real-Time, Photo-Realistic and Closed-Loop Simulator for Autonomous Driving
output: real-time closed-loop 3DGS driving simulator with Gymnasium API and reactive actors
evaluation: Benchmarks end-to-end planners (UniAD, VAD, Latent TransFuser) in closed loop over 70+ sequences from KITTI-360, Waymo, nuScenes and PandaSet with 400+ scenarios.

generalization.note: Ego and actors move off the logged trajectories under control commands, with normal and aggressive actor behaviours.

summary: Closed-loop, photo-realistic simulator that lifts driving images into 3DGS and lets autonomous-driving algorithms drive inside reconstructed scenes.
how: Holistic 3DGS reconstruction from RGB and noisy 2D/3D predictions handles viewpoint extrapolation and 360-degree vehicles; a simulation loop updates ego and actor states from control commands.

name: ChatSim
title: Editable Scene Simulation for Autonomous Driving via Collaborative LLM-Agents
output: language-editable photo-realistic multi-camera driving scene simulation with inserted 3D assets
evaluation: Evaluates rendering quality and lighting estimation on Waymo, a user study on edited scenes, and simulated data as augmentation for 3D detection (Lift-Splat).

generalization.note: Produces edited scenes not in the log (added, removed, moved vehicles, new viewpoints), but no closed-loop driving.

summary: Collaborating LLM agents turn natural-language commands into edits of a reconstructed driving scene, rendering photo-realistic multi-camera results with external assets.
how: LLM agents decompose commands into view, background, asset and motion tasks; a multi-camera NeRF renders the background and inserted assets are lit with estimated scene lighting.

name: S3Gaussian
title: S³Gaussian: Self-Supervised Street Gaussians for Autonomous Driving
output: annotation-free 4D Gaussian street scene for driving simulation
evaluation: Measures scene reconstruction and novel-view synthesis on Waymo Open against box-supervised and self-supervised baselines.

generalization.note: Only held-out frames and views from the recorded log are evaluated.

summary: Self-supervised street Gaussians that separate static and dynamic content from 4D consistency, avoiding costly tracked 3D boxes.
how: Scenes are 3D Gaussians plus a spatial-temporal field network modelling 4D deformation; static/dynamic decomposition emerges from reconstruction losses alone.

name: SplatAD
title: SplatAD: Real-Time Lidar and Camera Rendering with 3D Gaussian Splatting for Autonomous Driving
output: real-time 3DGS sensor simulator for both cameras and LiDAR
evaluation: Compares camera (PSNR) and LiDAR (Chamfer, intensity, ray drop) rendering quality and speed on PandaSet, Argoverse 2 and nuScenes.

generalization.note: Supports actor and ego edits like NeuRAD, but metrics are on held-out log data.

summary: First 3DGS method to render both camera and LiDAR in real time, modelling rolling shutter, LiDAR intensity and ray dropouts.
how: Dynamic 3DGS scenes with actor boxes are rasterized by purpose-built camera and spherical LiDAR projections with sensor effects, optimized jointly on both modalities.

name: DriveDreamer4D
title: DriveDreamer4D: World Models Are Effective Data Machines for 4D Driving Scene Representation
output: 4DGS driving scene that renders novel ego trajectories (lane changes, speed changes)
evaluation: Measures rendering on novel trajectories with FID, NTA-IoU and NTL-IoU on Waymo, plus a user study, against PVG, S3Gaussian and Deformable-GS.

generalization.note: Explicitly evaluates rendering along ego trajectories that never occurred in the log.

summary: Uses a driving world model as a data machine to synthesize novel-trajectory videos that improve 4D Gaussian reconstruction for closed-loop simulation.
how: A structure-conditioned video world model generates videos along edited ego trajectories; these 'cousin' data are mixed with real logs to train the 4D Gaussian scene.

name: ReconDreamer
title: ReconDreamer: Crafting World Models for Driving Scene Reconstruction via Online Restoration
output: Gaussian driving scene that stays photo-realistic under large maneuvers (multi-lane shifts)
evaluation: Evaluates novel-trajectory rendering on Waymo with NTA-IoU, NTL-IoU, FID and a user study, at lane shifts up to 6 m.

generalization.note: Targets and measures rendering quality on large ego maneuvers outside the logged trajectory.

summary: Incrementally injects world-model knowledge into driving-scene reconstruction so it can render large maneuvers like multi-lane shifts.
how: A video-diffusion restorer (DriveRestorer) cleans artifacts in renders from novel trajectories online, and a progressive data update feeds restored views back into Gaussian training.

name: NeuroNCAP
title: NeuroNCAP: Photorealistic Closed-loop Safety Testing for Autonomous Driving
output: NeRF-based closed-loop simulator and safety-critical scenario suite for end-to-end planners
evaluation: Tests end-to-end planners (UniAD, VAD) in closed loop on Euro NCAP-inspired stationary, frontal and side collision scenarios built from nuScenes, scoring collision avoidance.

generalization.note: Inserts and reroutes actors into new safety-critical scenarios and lets the planner drive the ego vehicle in closed loop.

summary: Sensor-realistic closed-loop testbed that reconfigures reconstructed real driving logs into Euro NCAP-style safety-critical scenarios for end-to-end planners.
how: Real nuScenes sequences are reconstructed with NeuRAD; actors are inserted on collision courses and the planner's outputs drive the ego through a controller in a render-plan-act loop.

name: RAD
title: RAD: Training an End-to-End Driving Policy via Large-Scale 3DGS-based Reinforcement Learning
institution: Huazhong University of Science and Technology
output: large-scale 3DGS digital replicas of real driving clips used as RL training and evaluation environments
evaluation: Trains and evaluates an end-to-end policy in closed loop on unseen 3DGS environments, reporting collision rate and other closed-loop metrics against IL baselines.

generalization.note: The policy explores freely and is tested in closed loop on held-out reconstructed environments.

summary: Builds photorealistic 3DGS replicas of real driving data and trains an end-to-end driving policy in them with reinforcement learning.
how: Real clips are reconstructed with 3DGS; the policy acts in the replicas via a kinematic bicycle model with safety-oriented rewards and IL regularization, while other traffic is log-replayed.

name: RealEngine
title: RealEngine: Simulating Autonomous Driving in Realistic Context
output: closed-loop multi-agent driving simulator with reconstructed backgrounds and recomposable traffic participants (camera + LiDAR)
evaluation: Evaluates rendering realism and runs non-reactive, safety-testing and multi-agent interaction simulations of driving agents on recomposed real scenes.

generalization.note: Traffic participants are recombined into new scenarios and agents drive free-form trajectories in closed loop.

summary: Driving simulation framework that reconstructs real backgrounds and traffic participants separately so they can be recombined into diverse closed-loop scenarios.
how: Background scenes and foreground actors are reconstructed from multi-modal logs and recomposed; novel-view synthesis renders camera and LiDAR for each agent step.

name: World Engine
title: World Engine: Towards the Era of Post-Training for Autonomous Driving
output: interactive 3DGS environments of real failure scenarios with generated safety-critical behaviour variants
evaluation: Post-trains planners with RL and measures closed-loop success on safety-critical nuPlan scenarios, plus a production simulator and on-road tests.

generalization.note: Scenes are extrapolated into adversarial behaviour variations and policies are tested in closed loop and on the road.

summary: Reconstructs failure-prone real driving logs into interactive neural worlds and extrapolates them into safety-critical variants for RL post-training of driving policies.
how: Failure scenarios are reconstructed with 3D Gaussian Splatting; a generative behaviour world model creates adversarial actor variations used for reinforcement post-training.

name: Instant NuRec
title: Instant NuRec: Feed-Forward 3D Gaussian Reconstruction for Driving Scene Simulation
output: simulatable layered 3DGS world (static, dynamic, sky, per-camera ISP) from a short multi-camera log
evaluation: Reports PSNR on Waymo Open, detection precision/recall on renders and reconstruction time, and runs closed-loop policy rollouts in AlpaSim (collision and off-road rates).

generalization.note: Reconstructions are driven in closed loop by several policies under different camera configurations.

summary: Feed-forward model that turns a 10-20 s multi-camera driving log into a simulatable 3DGS world in about 1.5 seconds.
how: A single forward pass predicts static and dynamic 3DGS layers, a sky cubemap and per-camera ISP corrections, with non-pinhole cameras via 3DGUT, plugging into NuRec and AlpaSim.

name: RECAST
title: RECAST: From Log Replay to Closed-Loop Driving Simulation with View-Complete Actors
output: reconstructed driving scene with generated view-complete 3DGS vehicles for planner-in-the-loop simulation
evaluation: Measures actor and scene realism (FD, CLIP margin) under actor motion beyond logged trajectories and runs planner-in-the-loop tests with GTRS-Dense (no-collision rate, TTC).

generalization.note: Actors are moved beyond their logged trajectories and a planner drives in closed loop against them.

summary: Generates complete 3D vehicles from a single segmented log observation so actors look right from viewpoints the log never captured.
how: An image-to-3D prior (TRELLIS) adapted on the 20K-vehicle RECAR dataset generates each actor, which is registered into a Street Gaussians scene for closed-loop rendering.

name: NeuroFluid
title: NeuroFluid: Fluid Dynamics Grounding with Particle-Driven Neural Radiance Fields
output: fluid particles + learned particle transition model
evaluation: Novel-view rendering of observed frames and accuracy of inferred particle positions against simulator ground truth.

generalization.note: Mainly evaluated on the observed sequences; some tests vary initial fluid states.

summary: Grounds Lagrangian fluid particle dynamics in multi-view RGB video by driving a NeRF with simulated particles.
how: A particle transition model is trained end-to-end through a particle-driven neural renderer so rendered frames match the observed fluid video.

name: HyFluid
title: Inferring Hybrid Neural Fluid Fields from Videos
output: neural fluid density + divergence-free velocity fields
evaluation: Novel-view synthesis, re-simulation and future prediction of smoke against real captures.

generalization.note: Tested on re-simulation, future prediction and new views beyond the fitted frames.

summary: Recovers fluid density and a physically plausible velocity field from sparse multi-view smoke videos.
how: Physics losses enforce divergence-free velocity that transports density, with a hybrid base plus vortex velocity representation fitted to the videos.

name: DVP (Learning Vortex Dynamics)
title: Learning Vortex Dynamics for Fluid Inference and Prediction
output: vortex particles + differentiable vortex dynamics model
evaluation: Accuracy of inferred velocity fields and quality of future-frame prediction on synthetic and real fluid videos.

generalization.note: The fitted vortex model is rolled forward to predict fluid evolution beyond the observed clip.

summary: Infers and predicts fluid dynamics from a single 2D video using a differentiable vortex particle method.
how: A latent set of Lagrangian vortex particles is evolved by learnable vortex dynamics and optimized so advected images match the video.

name: FluidNexus
title: FluidNexus: 3D Fluid Reconstruction and Prediction from a Single Video
output: 3D fluid particles/fields + physics simulation for prediction
evaluation: Reconstruction and future prediction quality on real smoke datasets with multi-view held-out cameras.

generalization.note: Predicts future fluid motion and renders novel views not present in the single input video.

summary: Reconstructs and predicts 3D fluid motion from a single video by combining video generation with physics simulation.
how: A novel-view video synthesizer generates multi-view references, then a physics-integrated particle representation is optimized to them and rolled forward for prediction.

name: Vid2Fluid
title: Physics-Driven Extraction of Dynamic Fluid Asset from Monocular Video with Generative 3DGS
output: 3D fluid asset + fitted fluid simulator parameters
evaluation: Visual fidelity of re-simulated fluid against the input video and its use in new scenes.

generalization.note: The extracted fluid is re-simulated in edited scenes, but quantitative tests focus on the input videos.

summary: Extracts a re-simulatable 3D fluid asset from a single-view video by optimizing fluid simulator parameters to match the observed dynamics.
how: Generative 3DGS gives initial geometry, a physics-corrected velocity field is estimated from surface motion, and simulator parameters are optimized to reproduce the video.

name: LagrangianSplats
title: LagrangianSplats: Divergence-Free Transport of Gaussian Primitives for Fluid Reconstruction
output: Lagrangian 3D Gaussians + divergence-free velocity field
evaluation: Velocity and appearance reconstruction accuracy on synthetic and real fluid captures.

generalization.note: Evaluated on reconstructing the observed sequences.

summary: Reconstructs 3D fluid velocity from sparse 2D videos with a velocity representation that is divergence-free by construction.
how: A divergence-free kernel velocity field advects Lagrangian 3D Gaussians, optimized with a sliding-window scheme against the input views.

name: Cloth in the Wind
title: Cloth in the Wind: A Case Study of Physical Measurement through Simulation
output: cloth material parameters + wind force for a cloth simulator
evaluation: Accuracy of estimated wind speed against anemometer ground truth on real flag videos.

generalization.note: Measures parameters of the observed flags; no rollout under new conditions.

summary: Estimates cloth material properties and external wind force from real videos of flags by refining a cloth simulation.
how: A simulation is iteratively updated so a learned spectral embedding of simulated and real cloth motion becomes close.

name: DiffCloud
title: DiffCloud: Real-to-Sim from Point Clouds with Differentiable Simulation and Rendering of Deformable Objects
output: cloth simulation parameters (mass, stiffness)
evaluation: Chamfer distance between simulated and real point clouds for cloth lift and fold tasks.

generalization.note: Fits parameters to observed manipulation trajectories only.

summary: Infers deformable-object simulation parameters from real point clouds of a robot manipulating cloth.
how: A differentiable cloth simulator and differentiable point-cloud rendering let gradients of a Chamfer loss update mass and stiffness.

name: Gaussian Garments
title: Gaussian Garments: Reconstructing Simulation-Ready Clothing with Photorealistic Appearance from Multi-View Video
output: garment mesh + Gaussian texture + garment-specific fine-tuned GNN simulator
evaluation: Appearance and geometry fidelity of reconstructed garments and plausibility of their simulated motion.

generalization.note: Garments are animated in new poses and combined into new multi-layer outfits.

summary: Reconstructs simulation-ready garments with photorealistic appearance from multi-view video, with behavior tuned to each real garment.
how: Mesh plus Gaussian texture is registered to the videos, and a pre-trained GNN cloth simulator is fine-tuned to replicate the garment's observed motion.

name: NeuPhysics
title: NeuPhysics: Editable Neural Geometry and Physics from Monocular Videos
output: SDF geometry + hexahedral mesh + elastic physics parameters
evaluation: Recovery of physical parameters and re-rendering of edited or re-simulated motion.

generalization.note: Shows edits of physical parameters and new interactions, but numbers are on the fitted scenes.

summary: Learns 3D geometry and physical parameters of a dynamic scene from a single monocular video, enabling physics edits.
how: A time-invariant SDF plus deformation field is bridged to a differentiable mesh simulator whose parameters are fitted to the video.

name: NVFi
title: NVFi: Neural Velocity Fields for 3D Physics Learning from Dynamic Videos
output: keyframe neural geometry/appearance + physics-constrained velocity field
evaluation: Future frame extrapolation, semantic scene decomposition and motion transfer on synthetic and real data.

generalization.note: Evaluated on extrapolating frames beyond the training time window.

summary: Learns geometry, appearance and a 3D velocity field from multi-view videos so the scene can be extrapolated into the future.
how: A velocity field is trained with physics-informed (Navier-Stokes style) constraints together with a keyframe radiance field.

name: FreeGave
title: FreeGave: 3D Physics Learning from Dynamic Videos by Gaussian Velocity
output: 3D Gaussians + divergence-free Gaussian velocity field
evaluation: Future frame extrapolation and motion segmentation on synthetic and real datasets.

generalization.note: Predicts frames beyond the observed time range.

summary: Learns 3D scene physics from multi-view dynamic videos without object priors by attaching velocities to Gaussians.
how: A divergence-free module estimates per-Gaussian velocity, avoiding PINN losses, and is fitted to the videos for extrapolation.

name: TRACE
title: TRACE: Learning 3D Gaussian Physical Dynamics from Multi-view Videos
output: 3D Gaussians as rigid particles with learned translation/rotation dynamics parameters
evaluation: Future frame extrapolation and unsupervised object segmentation by learned physical parameters.

generalization.note: Evaluated on extrapolating dynamics beyond the observed frames.

summary: Models a dynamic 3D scene as Gaussians with learned rigid-particle dynamics, enabling future prediction without labels.
how: Each Gaussian is treated as a rigid particle in space whose translation and rotation dynamics parameters are learned from the videos.

name: PAIG (Physics-as-Inverse-Graphics)
title: Physics-as-Inverse-Graphics: Unsupervised Physical Parameter Estimation from Video
output: object states + explicit physical parameters in a differentiable physics engine
evaluation: Long-term video prediction and recovered physical parameters on synthetic videos of interacting objects.

generalization.note: Extrapolates far beyond training horizons and supports vision-based model-predictive control.

summary: Learns objects, their states and explicit physical parameters from video without supervision via a differentiable physics engine.
how: An encoder recovers object positions, a differentiable physics engine with learnable parameters rolls them forward, and a decoder renders frames back.

name: VRDP
title: Dynamic Visual Reasoning by Learning Differentiable Physics Models from Video and Language
output: object trajectories + physical parameters (mass, friction, restitution) in a differentiable simulator
evaluation: Question-answering accuracy on CLEVRER and Real-Billiard, including predictive and counterfactual questions.

generalization.note: Answers counterfactual and predictive questions by re-simulating with the fitted physics.

summary: Jointly learns visual concepts and infers object physics from video and language through a differentiable physics model.
how: Perception and concept learners recover objects; an impulse-based differentiable rigid-body simulator fits their physical parameters to observed trajectories.

name: D-REX
title: D-REX: Differentiable Real-to-Sim-to-Real Engine for Learning Dexterous Grasping
output: Gaussian-splat object twin + identified object mass in a differentiable engine
evaluation: Mass identification accuracy and real-robot force-aware grasping success.

generalization.note: Identified twins are used to train grasping policies deployed on a real robot.

summary: Identifies object mass from visual observations and robot control signals with a Gaussian-splat differentiable engine, then learns force-aware grasping.
how: Gaussian splats give geometry; a differentiable physics engine optimizes mass so simulated motion matches observed robot-object interaction.

name: Physically Embodied Gaussian Splatting
title: Physically Embodied Gaussian Splatting: A Realtime Correctable World Model for Robotics
output: particles with physics (particle-based simulation) + attached 3D Gaussians
evaluation: Tracking accuracy of the simulated state against real multi-camera observations in real time.

generalization.note: Predicts forward states in real time but is continuously corrected by observations.

summary: A dual Gaussian-particle world model that simulates physics and is corrected online from camera images in real time.
how: Particles run in a particle-based physics system; differences between rendered Gaussians and observed images produce corrective forces.

name: BlenderAlchemy
title: BlenderAlchemy: Editing 3D Graphics with Vision-Language Models
output: edited Blender Python programs (materials, geometry, lighting)
evaluation: Match of rendered results to reference images and text intents, judged by humans and VLMs.

generalization.note: Each program is edited for its own target.

summary: A VLM system that edits Blender programs to match text and reference images.
how: A vision-based edit generator proposes Blender code edits and a VLM state evaluator selects the best renders iteratively.

name: SceneScript
title: SceneScript: Reconstructing Scenes With An Autoregressive Structured Language Model
output: structured scene-language command sequence (walls, doors, windows, object boxes)
evaluation: Layout estimation and 3D object detection accuracy on synthetic and real egocentric scans.

generalization.note: Trained on synthetic scenes and tested on real-world captures.

summary: Reconstructs indoor scenes as a sequence of structured language commands predicted from egocentric video.
how: An encoder-decoder model autoregressively emits scene commands from point clouds or video features, trained on the Aria Synthetic Environments dataset.

name: The Scene Language
title: The Scene Language: Representing Scenes with Programs, Words, and Embeddings
output: scene program + words + embeddings, rendered by multiple engines
evaluation: Quality and prompt fidelity of generated 3D/4D scenes, including image-conditioned generation, via user studies and metrics.

generalization.note: Programs can be edited and re-rendered with different renderers.

summary: Represents visual scenes as programs, words and embeddings, inferred by an LLM from text or images.
how: A pre-trained LLM writes the scene program and words; embeddings capture identity; outputs render through traditional, neural or mixed graphics.

name: Video2Game
title: Video2Game: Real-time, Interactive, Realistic and Browser-Compatible Environment from a Single Video
output: browser-runnable interactive game environment (meshes, textures, rigid-body physics)
evaluation: Rendering quality and real-time interactivity on indoor and outdoor scenes.

generalization.note: The resulting game supports new interactions, but evaluation centers on rendering.

summary: Turns a single video of a scene into a real-time, interactive, browser-compatible game environment with physics.
how: A NeRF is distilled into textured meshes, decomposed into actionable entities with collision geometry, and assembled in a WebGL game engine with physics.

name: 3D-CoS
title: 3D-CoS: A New 3D Reconstruction Paradigm Based on VLM Code Synthesis
output: executable Blender Python code reconstructing the object
evaluation: Reconstruction fidelity of code-built objects and quality of localized code edits versus mesh and point-cloud baselines.

generalization.note: Tests localized text-driven edits of the reconstructed program.

summary: Studies reconstructing 3D objects as executable Blender code written by VLMs, with structured synthesis workflows.
how: VLMs write Blender code using blueprint planning, RAG over the Blender API, few-shot examples, and part-wise agent workflows.

name: Agentic Real2Sim
title: Agentic Real2Sim: Physics-based World Modeling with Vision-Language Agents
output: MuJoCo episode twin (scene, objects, poses, robot motion, physical properties)
evaluation: Conversion success rate and use of twins for policy fine-tuning and as a surrogate for real-world policy evaluation.

generalization.note: Converted twins are used for policy fine-tuning and evaluation beyond the recorded episode.

summary: Vision-language agents convert recordings of robot-object interaction into runnable MuJoCo episode twins.
how: Agents orchestrate perception tools to recover geometry, poses, motion and physical properties, assemble them in MuJoCo and refine in simulation.

name: Real2Gym
title: Real2Gym: Building Gyms from Videos, Bringing Skills to Robots
output: editable Blender/MuJoCo simulation gyms + executable manipulation code
evaluation: Simulation task success and real Franka robot execution success with skills learned in the gyms.

generalization.note: Generates task-conditioned variations and transfers skills to a real robot.

summary: An agentic Real2Sim2Real framework that turns demonstration videos into interactive simulation gyms and transfers learned skills to robots.
how: Scenes are reconstructed and aligned to the video, demonstrated actions are validated in native physics, and an agent writes and refines manipulation code.

name: RoboSimStudio
title: RoboSimStudio: An Interactive Toolkit for Human and Agent Rapid Real2Sim of Robot Manipulation Tasks
output: editable Newton multi-physics simulation (solver, contact model, parameters)
evaluation: Visual and force-feedback agreement with real behavior and agentic Real2Sim2Real experiments.

generalization.note: Simulations are refined against observed behavior and used for Real2Sim2Real transfer.

summary: A toolkit that makes simulation choices explicit and editable so humans or coding agents can quickly build manipulation simulations from observations.
how: Built on the Newton physics system; humans or coding agents iteratively edit solver, contact model and parameters to match observed behavior.

name: SceneAgent
title: SceneAgent: An Agentic Pipeline from 3D and 4D Captures to Simulation Environments
output: interactive simulation environment with articulated and deformable objects
evaluation: Reconstruction F1 on a cluttered bin scene and dynamic IoU on 4DCodeBench dynamic scenes.

generalization.note: Generates object variants and shows preliminary real-robot policy transfer.

summary: An agentic pipeline that converts 3DGS, photogrammetry, LiDAR and 4D video captures into simulation environments with simulator-based repair.
how: Coding agents chain segmentation, physical parameter estimation, part decomposition, articulation and deformable simulation, inspecting the simulator to fix errors.

name: BlenderGym
title: BlenderGym: Benchmarking Foundational Model Systems for Graphics Editing
target_output: edited Blender Python program whose render matches a goal image
scale: Blender reconstruction tasks across geometry, material, lighting, blend shape and placement
evaluation: Renders of the edited program are compared with the goal image by photometric and perceptual metrics.

generalization.note: Each task is scored on its own target image.

summary: A benchmark of code-based 3D reconstruction tasks where VLM systems edit Blender programs to match target images.
how: Start and goal scenes are given as Blender code and renders; systems must output code that reproduces the goal render.

name: IR3D-Bench
title: IR3D-Bench: Evaluating Vision-Language Model Scene Understanding as Agentic Inverse Rendering
target_output: Blender Python script (via MCP) that recreates the 3D scene of an input image
scale: CLEVR-style scenes
evaluation: Recreated scenes are scored for geometric accuracy, spatial relations, appearance attributes and overall plausibility.

generalization.note: Each image is reconstructed independently.

summary: A benchmark asking vision-language agents to recreate the 3D structure of an image by writing and rendering Blender scripts.
how: Agents write Python scripts sent to Blender through the Model Context Protocol; outputs are matched to ground-truth scene objects.

name: SceneActBench
title: SceneActBench: Can Agents Act on the 3D Scenes They See?
target_output: final 3D scene state produced by acting in a headless Blender environment
scale: 520 task cases from 210 source instances across 5 tasks
evaluation: Final scenes are compared with hidden ground truth using task-specific geometric metrics.

generalization.note: Each case is scored against its own hidden ground truth.

summary: A benchmark where VLM agents act on full 3D scenes in Blender from images or video frames across layout, camera, reconstruction, articulation and dynamics tasks.
how: All tasks run through one fixed agent loop with a shared tool interface; outputs are measured geometrically against ground truth.

name: CineRecon
title: CineRecon: Benchmarking Frontier Models for Agentic Cinematic Reconstruction
target_output: editable dynamic 3D scene (animated, rendered) reproducing the reference video
scale: 50 reference videos, 360 annotated clips
evaluation: A VLM judge checks timestamp-aligned reference and rendered frames against checklists across camera, static and dynamic consistency.

generalization.note: Reconstructions are compared only with their own reference clips.

summary: A benchmark for agents that reconstruct film, real and game videos as editable, animated 3D scenes.
how: Agents use tools to build, animate, render and refine scenes under Proxy, Simplified and Detailed representation settings.
